Plot fitted trans functions and/or their derivatives.

Simple plot showing just the fitted Hill functions (no smoothed data). Useful for comparing multiple genes or viewing function shape with derivatives.

Parameters
  • model (bayesDREAM): Model with fit_trans() completed
  • features (str or list of str): Single feature name or list of feature names to plot
  • modality_name (str, optional): Modality name (default: primary modality)
  • show_function (bool): Show the fitted function y(x) (default: True)
  • show_first_derivative (bool): Show first derivative dy/dx (default: False)
  • show_second_derivative (bool): Show second derivative d²y/dx² (default: False)
  • show_third_derivative (bool): Show second derivative d3y/dx3 (default: False)
  • x_range (np.ndarray, optional): X values to plot at. If None, generates evenly spaced points in log2 space from model's x_true range.
  • n_points (int): Number of points for x_range if auto-generated (default: 2000). Points are evenly spaced in log2 space for smooth curves on log-log plots.
  • use_log2_x (bool): Use log2(x) for x-axis (default: True). Ignored if use_log2fc=True.
  • use_log2fc (bool): If True, plot in log2 fold-change space relative to NTC (default: False).
    • x-axis: log2FC = log2(x) - log2(x_ntc) where x_ntc is cis gene NTC mean
    • y-axis: log2FC = log2(y) - log2(y_ntc) where y_ntc is trans gene NTC mean
    • Derivatives: dg/du and d²g/du² (chain rule transformed) Requires posterior_samples_ntc to be available for both cis and trans modalities. Not recommended for binomial modalities (use use_delta_p instead).
  • use_delta_p (bool): If True, plot in probability difference space relative to NTC (default: False). Designed for binomial modalities (e.g., splicing_sj).
    • x-axis: log2FC = log2(x) - log2(x_ntc) where x_ntc is cis gene NTC mean
    • y-axis: Δp = p - p_ntc where p is probability and p_ntc is NTC probability
    • Derivatives: dp/du and d²p/du² (chain rule transformed) Requires posterior_samples_ntc to be available for both cis and trans modalities. Mutually exclusive with use_log2fc.
  • show_posterior_samples (bool): If True, plot individual posterior fits behind the mean line (default: False). Each posterior sample is plotted with transparency set by posterior_alpha.
  • show_ci (bool): If True, show 95% credible interval band around the mean line (default: False). The CI is computed at each x point and shown as a shaded region.
  • posterior_alpha (float): Transparency for individual posterior sample lines (default: 0.1). Only used when show_posterior_samples=True.
  • ci_alpha (float): Transparency for the 95% CI shaded region (default: 0.3). Only used when show_ci=True.
  • max_posterior_samples (int): Maximum number of posterior samples to plot (default: 1000). Only used when show_posterior_samples=True.
  • colors (str, list, or dict, optional): Colors for each feature. Can be:
    • Single color string (all features same color)
    • List of colors (one per feature)
    • Dict mapping feature names to colors If None, uses default color cycle.
  • alpha (float): Line transparency (default: 0.8)
  • linewidth (float): Line width (default: 1.5)
  • figsize (tuple, optional): Figure size (width, height). Auto-sized if None.
  • title (str, optional): Plot title. If None, auto-generated.
  • legend (bool): Show legend (default: True)
  • ax (plt.Axes, optional): Existing axes to plot on. If None, creates new figure.

  • overlay_roots (pd.DataFrame, pd.Series, dict, or None): If provided, draws dashed vertical lines at derivative roots on each subplot. Accepted forms:

    • pd.DataFrame (full summary from save_trans_summary): for each feature being plotted, the matching row is looked up by the feature column.
    • pd.Series / dict (a single row): used as-is for every feature.
    • None (default): no overlay.

    Root columns are selected automatically to match the plot's x-axis space: *_log2fc_mean when use_log2fc=True, *_delta_p_mean when use_delta_p=True, and *_mean (x-space, converted to log2 if use_log2_x=True) otherwise.

  • overlay_roots_lw (float): Line width for root vlines (default 1.0).
  • overlay_roots_alpha (float): Transparency for root vlines (default 0.8).
  • overlay_roots_also_on_function (bool): If True (default), draw all root sets also on the function subplot.
  • fdr_threshold (float, default 0.05): For additive_hill: FDR-inactive components (q-value >= fdr_threshold) are gated to zero in the plotted curve/derivatives, consistent with _compute_hill_markers, predict_hill_from_summary_row, and save_trans_summary's point estimates.
  • fdr_df (pd.DataFrame, optional): Precomputed trans_summary DataFrame to source activity calls from, instead of recomputing Bayesian FDR live from the posterior for each feature.
Returns
  • plt.Figure: Matplotlib figure
Raises
  • ValueError: If function type is polynomial (derivatives not supported) If no features could be plotted If use_log2fc=True but NTC means not available If use_delta_p=True but NTC means not available If both use_log2fc and use_delta_p are True (mutually exclusive)
Examples
>>> # Plot function and derivatives for one gene
>>> model.plot_trans_functions('TET2', show_first_derivative=True,
...                            show_second_derivative=True)

>>> # Plot with derivative roots overlaid from summary df
>>> df = model.save_trans_summary(compute_derivative_roots=True)
>>> model.plot_trans_functions('TET2', use_log2fc=True,
...                            show_function=True,
...                            show_first_derivative=True,
...                            show_second_derivative=True,
...                            show_third_derivative=True,
...                            overlay_roots=df)

>>> # Plot first derivative of multiple genes
>>> model.plot_trans_functions(['TET2', 'MYB', 'GFI1B'],
...                            show_function=False,
...                            show_first_derivative=True)

>>> # Plot all non-monotonic genes (genes where derivative changes sign)
>>> feature_names = model.get_modality(model.primary_modality).feature_names
>>> non_monotonic = [g for g in feature_names if is_non_monotonic(model, g)]
>>> model.plot_trans_functions(non_monotonic, show_first_derivative=True)
def predict_trans_function( model, feature: str, x_range: numpy.ndarray, modality_name: Optional[str] = None, fdr_threshold: float = 0.05, fdr_df: Optional[pandas.core.frame.DataFrame] = None, debug: bool = False) -> Optional[numpy.ndarray]: 
2308def predict_trans_function(
2309    model,
2310    feature: str,
2311    x_range: np.ndarray,
2312    modality_name: Optional[str] = None,
2313    fdr_threshold: float = 0.05,
2314    fdr_df: Optional["pd.DataFrame"] = None,
2315    debug: bool = False
2316) -> Optional[np.ndarray]:
2317    """
2318    Predict trans effect function for a feature given x_true values.
2319
2320    Automatically detects function type (additive_hill, single_hill, polynomial)
2321    from posterior_samples_trans and computes predictions.
2322
2323    Parameters
2324    ----------
2325    model : bayesDREAM
2326        Model with fit_trans() completed
2327    feature : str
2328        Feature name to predict
2329    x_range : np.ndarray
2330        X values to predict at (cis expression levels)
2331    modality_name : str, optional
2332        Modality name (default: primary modality)
2333    fdr_threshold : float, default 0.05
2334        For additive_hill: components with Bayesian q-value >= fdr_threshold are
2335        FDR-inactive and gated to zero, so the curve reflects only statistically
2336        significant components — consistent with _compute_hill_markers,
2337        predict_hill_from_summary_row, and save_trans_summary's
2338        full_log2fc/observed_log2fc point estimates. Without gating, alpha/beta
2339        for null components are ~0.4-0.5 (RelaxedBernoulli prior) rather than 0,
2340        producing a spurious partial Hill contribution.
2341    fdr_df : pd.DataFrame, optional
2342        Precomputed trans_summary DataFrame (with fdr_alpha/fdr_beta columns) to
2343        source activity calls from, instead of recomputing Bayesian FDR live from
2344        the posterior on every call.
2345
2346    Returns
2347    -------
2348    np.ndarray or None
2349        Predicted y values at x_range, or None if:
2350        - Trans model not fitted
2351        - Feature not in trans_genes
2352        - Cannot determine function type
2353
2354    Notes
2355    -----
2356    Works with all function types:
2357    - additive_hill: A + alpha*Hill_a + beta*Hill_b
2358    - single_hill: A + Vmax*Hill(x, K, n)
2359    - polynomial: sum(coeffs[i] * x^i)
2360    """
2361    # Determine which modality to use
2362    if modality_name is None:
2363        modality_name = model.primary_modality
2364
2365    # Check if trans model fitted for this modality
2366    if modality_name == model.primary_modality:
2367        # Primary modality: check model-level posterior
2368        if not hasattr(model, 'posterior_samples_trans') or model.posterior_samples_trans is None:
2369            if debug: print(f"[predict_trans_function] returning None: no posterior_samples_trans on model")
2370            return None
2371        posterior = model.posterior_samples_trans
2372    else:
2373        # Non-primary modality: check modality-level posterior
2374        modality = model.get_modality(modality_name)
2375        if not hasattr(modality, 'posterior_samples_trans') or modality.posterior_samples_trans is None:
2376            if debug: print(f"[predict_trans_function] returning None: no posterior_samples_trans on modality '{modality_name}'")
2377            return None
2378        posterior = modality.posterior_samples_trans
2379
2380    if debug:
2381        print(f"[predict_trans_function] posterior keys: {list(posterior.keys())}")
2382
2383    # Get baseline A (present in all function types)
2384    if 'A' not in posterior:
2385        if debug: print(f"[predict_trans_function] returning None: 'A' not in posterior keys {list(posterior.keys())}")
2386        return None
2387
2388    A_samples = posterior['A']
2389
2390    # Get posterior dimensions
2391    # For primary modality: A_samples is (S, T) where S=samples, T=trans_genes
2392    #   After mean(dim=0): (T,)
2393    # For non-primary modality: A_samples is (S, C, T) where C=cis_genes, T=trans_features
2394    #   After mean(dim=0): (C, T)
2395    # We want the LAST dimension (T) in both cases
2396    if hasattr(A_samples, 'mean'):
2397        A_mean = A_samples.mean(dim=0)
2398        # Squeeze out cis gene dimension if present (should be size 1 for non-primary modalities)
2399        if A_mean.ndim > 1:
2400            A_mean = A_mean.squeeze(0)
2401        n_genes_posterior = A_mean.shape[0]
2402    else:
2403        A_mean = A_samples.mean(axis=0)
2404        # Squeeze out cis gene dimension if present
2405        if A_mean.ndim > 1:
2406            A_mean = A_mean.squeeze(0)
2407        n_genes_posterior = A_mean.shape[0]
2408
2409    # Get feature list from modality — always the ground truth.
2410    # modality.feature_names is the single source of truth (resolved + deduped
2411    # in Modality.__init__), no need to re-derive it here.
2412    modality = model.get_modality(modality_name)
2413    feature_list = modality.feature_names if modality.feature_names is not None else []
2414    if not feature_list and modality_name != model.primary_modality:
2415        if debug: print(f"[predict_trans_function] returning None: non-primary modality has no feature_names or feature_meta")
2416        return None
2417
2418    n_features_list = len(feature_list)
2419
2420    if debug:
2421        print(f"[predict_trans_function] n_genes_posterior={n_genes_posterior}, n_features_list={n_features_list}")
2422        print(f"[predict_trans_function] feature_list[:5]={feature_list[:5]}, ..., feature_list[-5:]={feature_list[-5:]}")
2423
2424    # Check dimension consistency BEFORE using feature_list for indexing
2425    if n_genes_posterior != n_features_list:
2426        # Mismatch - cannot use feature_list for indexing
2427        # This happens when posterior was fitted on a subset of features
2428        if debug: print(f"[predict_trans_function] returning None: dimension mismatch n_genes_posterior={n_genes_posterior} != n_features_list={n_features_list}")
2429        return None
2430
2431    # Now safe to check if feature is in feature_list and get its index
2432    if feature not in feature_list:
2433        if debug: print(f"[predict_trans_function] returning None: '{feature}' not in feature_list (len={n_features_list})")
2434        return None
2435
2436    feature_idx = feature_list.index(feature)
2437    A = A_mean[feature_idx].item() if hasattr(A_mean, 'item') else A_mean[feature_idx]
2438
2439    # Determine function type from available parameters
2440    if debug:
2441        print(f"[predict_trans_function] A={A_mean[feature_idx]:.4g}, feature_idx={feature_idx}")
2442        print(f"[predict_trans_function] branch check: Vmax_a={'Vmax_a' in posterior}, Vmax_b={'Vmax_b' in posterior}, upper_limit={'upper_limit' in posterior}, theta={'theta' in posterior}")
2443
2444    if 'Vmax_a' in posterior and 'Vmax_b' in posterior:
2445        # ===== ADDITIVE HILL (negbinom/normal/studentt) =====
2446        try:
2447            # Extract parameters using helper function
2448            alpha = _extract_param_mean(posterior['alpha'], feature_idx)
2449            beta = _extract_param_mean(posterior['beta'], feature_idx)
2450            Vmax_a = _extract_param_mean(posterior['Vmax_a'], feature_idx)
2451            Vmax_b = _extract_param_mean(posterior['Vmax_b'], feature_idx)
2452            K_a = _extract_param_mean(posterior['K_a'], feature_idx)
2453            K_b = _extract_param_mean(posterior['K_b'], feature_idx)
2454            n_a = _extract_param_mean(posterior['n_a'], feature_idx)
2455            n_b = _extract_param_mean(posterior['n_b'], feature_idx)
2456
2457            a_null, b_null = _resolve_hill_null_flags(
2458                feature, feature_idx, posterior, fdr_df=fdr_df, fdr_threshold=fdr_threshold
2459            )
2460            if a_null:
2461                alpha = 0.0
2462            if b_null:
2463                beta = 0.0
2464
2465            if debug:
2466                print(f"[predict_trans_function] additive_hill: A={A:.4g}, alpha={alpha:.4g}, beta={beta:.4g}, Vmax_a={Vmax_a:.4g}, Vmax_b={Vmax_b:.4g}, K_a={K_a:.4g}, K_b={K_b:.4g}, n_a={n_a:.4g}, n_b={n_b:.4g}")
2467
2468            # Compute Hill functions
2469            Hill_a = Hill_based_positive(x_range, Vmax=Vmax_a, A=0, K=K_a, n=n_a)
2470            Hill_b = Hill_based_positive(x_range, Vmax=Vmax_b, A=0, K=K_b, n=n_b)
2471
2472            # Combined prediction
2473            y_pred = A + alpha * Hill_a + beta * Hill_b
2474            if debug:
2475                print(f"[predict_trans_function] y_pred range: [{y_pred.min():.4g}, {y_pred.max():.4g}], any>0: {(y_pred > 0).any()}")
2476            return y_pred
2477
2478        except (KeyError, IndexError, AttributeError) as e:
2479            if debug: print(f"[predict_trans_function] returning None: additive_hill extraction failed: {e}")
2480            return None
2481
2482    elif 'upper_limit' in posterior and 'Vmax_a' in posterior and 'Vmax_b' in posterior:
2483        # ===== ADDITIVE HILL (binomial/multinomial with upper_limit and Vmax_a/b) =====
2484        try:
2485            # Extract parameters using helper function
2486            alpha = _extract_param_mean(posterior['alpha'], feature_idx)
2487            beta = _extract_param_mean(posterior['beta'], feature_idx)
2488            Vmax_a = _extract_param_mean(posterior['Vmax_a'], feature_idx)
2489            Vmax_b = _extract_param_mean(posterior['Vmax_b'], feature_idx)
2490            K_a = _extract_param_mean(posterior['K_a'], feature_idx)
2491            K_b = _extract_param_mean(posterior['K_b'], feature_idx)
2492            n_a = _extract_param_mean(posterior['n_a'], feature_idx)
2493            n_b = _extract_param_mean(posterior['n_b'], feature_idx)
2494
2495            a_null, b_null = _resolve_hill_null_flags(
2496                feature, feature_idx, posterior, fdr_df=fdr_df, fdr_threshold=fdr_threshold
2497            )
2498            if a_null:
2499                alpha = 0.0
2500            if b_null:
2501                beta = 0.0
2502
2503            # IMPORTANT: Match the actual model computation in fit_trans!
2504            # Model uses: y = A + (alpha * Hill_a(Vmax=Vmax_a)) + (beta * Hill_b(Vmax=Vmax_b))
2505            # where Hill functions return values in [0, Vmax]
2506            Hill_a = Hill_based_positive(x_range, Vmax=Vmax_a, A=0, K=K_a, n=n_a)
2507            Hill_b = Hill_based_positive(x_range, Vmax=Vmax_b, A=0, K=K_b, n=n_b)
2508
2509            # Combined prediction
2510            y_pred = A + alpha * Hill_a + beta * Hill_b
2511            return y_pred
2512
2513        except (KeyError, IndexError, AttributeError) as e:
2514            if debug: print(f"[predict_trans_function] returning None: upper_limit additive_hill extraction failed: {e}")
2515            return None
2516
2517    elif 'Vmax_a' in posterior:
2518        # ===== SINGLE HILL =====
2519        try:
2520            alpha = _extract_param_mean(posterior['alpha'], feature_idx)
2521            Vmax_a = _extract_param_mean(posterior['Vmax_a'], feature_idx)
2522            K_a = _extract_param_mean(posterior['K_a'], feature_idx)
2523            n_a = _extract_param_mean(posterior['n_a'], feature_idx)
2524
2525            # Compute Hill function: y = A + alpha * Hill(x, Vmax=Vmax_a, K=K_a, n=n_a)
2526            Hill_a = Hill_based_positive(x_range, Vmax=Vmax_a, A=0, K=K_a, n=n_a)
2527            y_pred = A + alpha * Hill_a
2528            return y_pred
2529
2530        except (KeyError, IndexError, AttributeError) as e:
2531            if debug: print(f"[predict_trans_function] returning None: single_hill extraction failed: {e}")
2532            return None
2533
2534    elif 'theta' in posterior:
2535        # ===== POLYNOMIAL OR THETA-BASED =====
2536        try:
2537            theta_samples = posterior['theta']
2538            # theta shape for primary: (samples, features, n_params)
2539            # theta shape for non-primary: (samples, cis_genes, features, n_params)
2540
2541            # Average over samples and squeeze cis gene dimension if present
2542            if hasattr(theta_samples, 'mean'):
2543                theta_mean = theta_samples.mean(dim=0)
2544                # Squeeze out cis gene dimension if present
2545                if theta_mean.ndim > 2:  # (cis_genes, features, n_params)
2546                    theta_mean = theta_mean.squeeze(0)  # (features, n_params)
2547                theta_mean = theta_mean[feature_idx, :]  # (n_params,)
2548                theta_np = theta_mean.cpu().numpy() if hasattr(theta_mean, 'cpu') else np.array(theta_mean)
2549            else:
2550                theta_mean = theta_samples.mean(axis=0)
2551                if theta_mean.ndim > 2:
2552                    theta_mean = theta_mean.squeeze(0)
2553                theta_mean = theta_mean[feature_idx, :]
2554                theta_np = np.array(theta_mean)
2555
2556            # Polynomial: y = coeffs[0] + coeffs[1]*x + coeffs[2]*x^2 + ...
2557            # First coefficient is baseline (like A)
2558            baseline = theta_np[0]
2559            poly_coeffs = theta_np[1:]  # Remaining coefficients
2560
2561            # Compute polynomial
2562            y_pred = np.full_like(x_range, baseline)
2563            for i, coeff in enumerate(poly_coeffs, start=1):
2564                y_pred += coeff * (x_range ** i)
2565
2566            return y_pred
2567
2568        except (KeyError, IndexError, AttributeError) as e:
2569            if debug: print(f"[predict_trans_function] returning None: polynomial extraction failed: {e}")
2570            return None
2571
2572    else:
2573        # Unknown function type
2574        if debug: print(f"[predict_trans_function] returning None: unrecognized function type (posterior keys: {list(posterior.keys())})")
2575        return None

Predict trans effect function for a feature given x_true values.

Automatically detects function type (additive_hill, single_hill, polynomial) from posterior_samples_trans and computes predictions.

Parameters
  • model (bayesDREAM): Model with fit_trans() completed
  • feature (str): Feature name to predict
  • x_range (np.ndarray): X values to predict at (cis expression levels)
  • modality_name (str, optional): Modality name (default: primary modality)
  • fdr_threshold (float, default 0.05): For additive_hill: components with Bayesian q-value >= fdr_threshold are FDR-inactive and gated to zero, so the curve reflects only statistically significant components — consistent with _compute_hill_markers, predict_hill_from_summary_row, and save_trans_summary's full_log2fc/observed_log2fc point estimates. Without gating, alpha/beta for null components are ~0.4-0.5 (RelaxedBernoulli prior) rather than 0, producing a spurious partial Hill contribution.
  • fdr_df (pd.DataFrame, optional): Precomputed trans_summary DataFrame (with fdr_alpha/fdr_beta columns) to source activity calls from, instead of recomputing Bayesian FDR live from the posterior on every call.
Returns
  • np.ndarray or None: Predicted y values at x_range, or None if:
    • Trans model not fitted
    • Feature not in trans_genes
    • Cannot determine function type
Notes

Works with all function types:

  • additive_hill: A + alphaHill_a + betaHill_b
  • single_hill: A + Vmax*Hill(x, K, n)
  • polynomial: sum(coeffs[i] * x^i)
def predict_hill_from_summary_row( row, x_range: numpy.ndarray, fdr_threshold: float = 0.05) -> Optional[numpy.ndarray]: 
2605def predict_hill_from_summary_row(row, x_range: np.ndarray, fdr_threshold: float = 0.05) -> Optional[np.ndarray]:
2606    """
2607    Compute a Hill curve from a trans_summary DataFrame row.
2608
2609    Supports both additive_hill (has Vmax_b_median) and single_hill rows.
2610    Parameters are read from columns named A_median, alpha_median, Vmax_a_median,
2611    K_a_median, n_a_median, beta_median, Vmax_b_median, K_b_median, n_b_median.
2612
2613    Gating: a component is zeroed out unless it's active — Bayesian q-value
2614    (fdr_alpha/fdr_beta) < fdr_threshold AND its Hill exponent's 95% CI
2615    (n_a_lower/n_a_upper, n_b_lower/n_b_upper) excludes 0 — so the curve reflects
2616    only components with an identified, statistically significant dose-response.
2617    Without gating, alpha/beta for null components are ~0.4-0.5 (RelaxedBernoulli
2618    prior) rather than 0, producing a spurious partial Hill contribution; the q-value
2619    alone would also let through alpha absorbing a constant offset while n ≈ 0
2620    (flat Hill, unidentified K). Matches active_a/active_b in io/summary.py and
2621    _resolve_hill_null_flags/_compute_hill_markers.
2622
2623    Returns y values at x_range, or None if required columns are missing.
2624    """
2625    def _g(col, default=None):
2626        v = row.get(col, default)
2627        try:
2628            v = float(v)
2629        except (TypeError, ValueError):
2630            return default
2631        return v if np.isfinite(v) else default
2632
2633    A       = _g('A_median', 0.0)
2634    alpha   = _g('alpha_median', 1.0)
2635    Vmax_a  = _g('Vmax_a_median')
2636    K_a     = _g('K_a_median')
2637    n_a     = _g('n_a_median')
2638    if Vmax_a is None or K_a is None or n_a is None:
2639        return None
2640
2641    if not _row_component_active(row, 'fdr_alpha', 'n_a_lower', 'n_a_upper', fdr_threshold):
2642        alpha = 0.0
2643
2644    Hill_a = Hill_based_positive(x_range, Vmax=Vmax_a, A=0, K=K_a, n=n_a)
2645    y_pred = A + alpha * Hill_a
2646
2647    beta   = _g('beta_median', 0.0)
2648    Vmax_b = _g('Vmax_b_median')
2649    K_b    = _g('K_b_median')
2650    n_b    = _g('n_b_median')
2651
2652    if not _row_component_active(row, 'fdr_beta', 'n_b_lower', 'n_b_upper', fdr_threshold):
2653        beta = 0.0
2654
2655    if Vmax_b is not None and K_b is not None and n_b is not None and beta != 0.0:
2656        Hill_b = Hill_based_positive(x_range, Vmax=Vmax_b, A=0, K=K_b, n=n_b)
2657        y_pred = y_pred + beta * Hill_b
2658
2659    return y_pred

Compute a Hill curve from a trans_summary DataFrame row.

Supports both additive_hill (has Vmax_b_median) and single_hill rows. Parameters are read from columns named A_median, alpha_median, Vmax_a_median, K_a_median, n_a_median, beta_median, Vmax_b_median, K_b_median, n_b_median.

Gating: a component is zeroed out unless it's active — Bayesian q-value (fdr_alpha/fdr_beta) < fdr_threshold AND its Hill exponent's 95% CI (n_a_lower/n_a_upper, n_b_lower/n_b_upper) excludes 0 — so the curve reflects only components with an identified, statistically significant dose-response. Without gating, alpha/beta for null components are ~0.4-0.5 (RelaxedBernoulli prior) rather than 0, producing a spurious partial Hill contribution; the q-value alone would also let through alpha absorbing a constant offset while n ≈ 0 (flat Hill, unidentified K). Matches active_a/active_b in io/summary.py and _resolve_hill_null_flags/_compute_hill_markers.

Returns y values at x_range, or None if required columns are missing.

def predict_trans_function_samples( model, feature: str, x_range: numpy.ndarray, modality_name: Optional[str] = None, max_samples: Optional[int] = None, fdr_threshold: float = 0.05, fdr_df: Optional[pandas.core.frame.DataFrame] = None) -> Optional[numpy.ndarray]: 
2662def predict_trans_function_samples(
2663    model,
2664    feature: str,
2665    x_range: np.ndarray,
2666    modality_name: Optional[str] = None,
2667    max_samples: Optional[int] = None,
2668    fdr_threshold: float = 0.05,
2669    fdr_df: Optional["pd.DataFrame"] = None,
2670) -> Optional[np.ndarray]:
2671    """
2672    Predict trans effect function for all posterior samples.
2673
2674    Like predict_trans_function but returns predictions for each posterior sample
2675    instead of just the mean.
2676
2677    Parameters
2678    ----------
2679    model : bayesDREAM
2680        Model with fit_trans() completed
2681    feature : str
2682        Feature name to predict
2683    x_range : np.ndarray
2684        X values to predict at (cis expression levels)
2685    modality_name : str, optional
2686        Modality name (default: primary modality)
2687    max_samples : int, optional
2688        Maximum number of samples to return. If None, returns all samples.
2689    fdr_threshold : float, default 0.05
2690        For additive_hill: FDR-inactive components (q-value >= fdr_threshold) are
2691        gated to zero for every sample, matching predict_trans_function so
2692        posterior-sample overlays and CI bands reflect the same gated curve as
2693        the mean line.
2694    fdr_df : pd.DataFrame, optional
2695        Precomputed trans_summary DataFrame to source activity calls from.
2696
2697    Returns
2698    -------
2699    np.ndarray or None
2700        Predicted y values with shape [n_samples, n_points], or None if prediction fails.
2701    """
2702    # Determine which modality to use
2703    if modality_name is None:
2704        modality_name = model.primary_modality
2705
2706    # Check if trans model fitted for this modality
2707    if modality_name == model.primary_modality:
2708        if not hasattr(model, 'posterior_samples_trans') or model.posterior_samples_trans is None:
2709            return None
2710        posterior = model.posterior_samples_trans
2711    else:
2712        modality = model.get_modality(modality_name)
2713        if not hasattr(modality, 'posterior_samples_trans') or modality.posterior_samples_trans is None:
2714            return None
2715        posterior = modality.posterior_samples_trans
2716
2717    # Get baseline A
2718    if 'A' not in posterior:
2719        return None
2720
2721    A_samples = posterior['A']
2722    if hasattr(A_samples, 'cpu'):
2723        A_samples = A_samples.cpu().numpy()
2724    else:
2725        A_samples = np.array(A_samples)
2726
2727    # Get feature list — always from the modality, never from model.trans_genes.
2728    # modality.feature_names is the single source of truth (resolved + deduped
2729    # in Modality.__init__), no need to re-derive it here.
2730    modality = model.get_modality(modality_name)
2731    feature_list = modality.feature_names
2732    if feature_list is None:
2733        return None
2734
2735    # Handle dimension squeezing for non-primary modalities
2736    # A_samples shape: (S, T) for primary, (S, C, T) for non-primary
2737    if A_samples.ndim > 2:
2738        A_samples = A_samples.squeeze(1)  # Remove cis gene dimension
2739
2740    # Get number of features in posterior
2741    n_features_posterior = A_samples.shape[1]
2742    n_features_list = len(feature_list)
2743
2744    # Check dimension consistency
2745    if n_features_posterior != n_features_list:
2746        # Mismatch - likely cis gene excluded from posterior
2747        # Try to find correct index by checking if cis gene is in list
2748        if hasattr(model, 'cis_gene') and model.cis_gene in feature_list:
2749            # Remove cis gene from feature list for indexing
2750            feature_list_adjusted = [f for f in feature_list if f != model.cis_gene]
2751            if feature not in feature_list_adjusted:
2752                return None
2753            if len(feature_list_adjusted) != n_features_posterior:
2754                return None  # Still mismatched
2755            feature_idx = feature_list_adjusted.index(feature)
2756        else:
2757            return None
2758    else:
2759        if feature not in feature_list:
2760            return None
2761        feature_idx = feature_list.index(feature)
2762
2763    # Determine function type and compute predictions
2764    if 'Vmax_a' in posterior and 'Vmax_b' in posterior:
2765        # ===== ADDITIVE HILL =====
2766        try:
2767            A = A_samples[:, feature_idx]  # [n_samples]
2768            alpha = _extract_param_samples(posterior, 'alpha', feature_idx)
2769            beta = _extract_param_samples(posterior, 'beta', feature_idx)
2770            Vmax_a = _extract_param_samples(posterior, 'Vmax_a', feature_idx)
2771            Vmax_b = _extract_param_samples(posterior, 'Vmax_b', feature_idx)
2772            K_a = _extract_param_samples(posterior, 'K_a', feature_idx)
2773            K_b = _extract_param_samples(posterior, 'K_b', feature_idx)
2774            n_a = _extract_param_samples(posterior, 'n_a', feature_idx)
2775            n_b = _extract_param_samples(posterior, 'n_b', feature_idx)
2776
2777            a_null, b_null = _resolve_hill_null_flags(
2778                feature, feature_idx, posterior, fdr_df=fdr_df, fdr_threshold=fdr_threshold
2779            )
2780            if a_null:
2781                alpha = np.zeros_like(alpha)
2782            if b_null:
2783                beta = np.zeros_like(beta)
2784
2785            n_samples = A.shape[0]
2786            if max_samples is not None and max_samples < n_samples:
2787                # Subsample
2788                indices = np.random.choice(n_samples, max_samples, replace=False)
2789                A = A[indices]
2790                alpha = alpha[indices]
2791                beta = beta[indices]
2792                Vmax_a = Vmax_a[indices]
2793                Vmax_b = Vmax_b[indices]
2794                K_a = K_a[indices]
2795                K_b = K_b[indices]
2796                n_a = n_a[indices]
2797                n_b = n_b[indices]
2798                n_samples = max_samples

2802            n_points = len(x_range)
2803            y_pred = np.zeros((n_samples, n_points))
2804
2805            for s in range(n_samples):

2808                y_pred[s, :] = A[s] + alpha[s] * Hill_a + beta[s] * Hill_b

2814
2815    elif 'Vmax_a' in posterior:
2816        # ===== SINGLE HILL =====
2817        try:
2818            A = A_samples[:, feature_idx]

2820            Vmax_a = _extract_param_samples(posterior, 'Vmax_a', feature_idx)

2822            n_a = _extract_param_samples(posterior, 'n_a', feature_idx)
2823
2824            n_samples = A.shape[0]

2827                A = A[indices]

2830                K_a = K_a[indices]

2839                y_pred[s, :] = A[s] + alpha[s] * Hill_a

2846    else:

Predict trans effect function for all posterior samples.

Like predict_trans_function but returns predictions for each posterior sample instead of just the mean.

Parameters

3691    Parameters (selected)
3692    ---------------------
3693    color_by : str or list of two str

3695        - ``'technical_group'`` (default): one line per cell-line / technical group
3696        - ``'targeting'``: two lines — NTC vs all targeting cells
3697        - Any column name in ``model.meta``: one line per unique value

3699          of two groupings. The first determines hue; the second determines shade — NTC gets
3700          a lighter tint of the group colour, Targeting gets the full colour.
3701
3702    Parameters
3703    ----------

3713    """
3714    # Get data
3715    feature_idx = _get_feature_index(feature, modality)
3716    if feature_idx is None:
3717        raise ValueError(f"Feature '{feature}' not found in modality")
3718
3719    # Get counts for this feature

3721        y_obs = modality.counts[feature_idx, :]
3722    else:
3723        y_obs = modality.counts[:, feature_idx]
3724

3730        )

3736

3738    df_data = {

3740        'y_obs': y_obs_aligned,

3743    }
3744

3748
3749    # Forward any extra meta columns referenced in color_by into df_data now,
3750    # before the DataFrame is built, so that the min_counts filter applies to them too.

3752    _SPECIAL_CB = {'technical_group', 'targeting'}

3758        # If not found anywhere, _resolve_grouping will warn later.
3759

3761
3762    # Filter by min_counts (exclude cells with raw counts below threshold)
3763    if min_counts > 0:
3764        df = df[df['y_obs'] >= min_counts].copy()
3765
3766    # Technical correction
3767    has_technical_fit = modality.alpha_y_prefit is not None
3768
3769    if show_correction == 'corrected' and not has_technical_fit:
3770        warnings.warn(f"Technical fit not available for modality '{modality.name}' - showing uncorrected only")
3771        show_correction = 'uncorrected'
3772

3777        else:
3778            fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1, figsize=figsize or (8, 5))
3779            axes = [ax]

3783        axes = [ax]

3793
3794    group_labels = [code_to_label[int(c)] for c in group_codes]

3815            x_ntc_valid = ntc_df['x_true'][ntc_df['x_true'] > 0]
3816            if len(x_ntc_valid) > 0:
3817                x_offset = np.log2(float(x_ntc_valid.mean()))
3818            else:
3819                warnings.warn("log2fc=True: no valid NTC cells found for x; plotting raw log2 instead.")
3820                x_offset = 0.0
3821            # y_offset: prefer mu_ntc from technical fit (same source as save_trans_summary).
3822            # mu_ntc is the model-inferred reference-group NTC expression rate [n_samples, T].
3823            # Fall back to empirical NTC reference-group mean when fit_technical not run.
3824            _feature_idx = _get_feature_index(feature, modality)
3825            _y_offset_from_technical = None
3826            if (_feature_idx is not None
3827                    and hasattr(modality, 'posterior_samples_ntc')
3828                    and modality.posterior_samples_ntc is not None
3829                    and 'mu_ntc' in modality.posterior_samples_ntc):
3830                _mu_ntc = modality.posterior_samples_ntc['mu_ntc']
3831                if hasattr(_mu_ntc, 'cpu'):
3832                    _mu_ntc = _mu_ntc.cpu().numpy()
3833                _mu_ntc = np.asarray(_mu_ntc, dtype=float)
3834                while _mu_ntc.ndim > 2:
3835                    _mu_ntc = _mu_ntc.mean(axis=0)
3836                _mu_ntc_mean = _mu_ntc.mean(axis=0)   # [T]
3837                if _feature_idx < len(_mu_ntc_mean):
3838                    _val = float(_mu_ntc_mean[_feature_idx])
3839                    if np.isfinite(_val) and _val > 0:
3840                        _y_offset_from_technical = np.log2(_val)
3841            if _y_offset_from_technical is not None:
3842                y_offset = _y_offset_from_technical
3843            else:
3844                # Empirical fallback: reference-group NTC mean
3845                if 'technical_group_code' in ntc_df.columns:
3846                    ntc_ref_df = ntc_df[ntc_df['technical_group_code'] == 0]
3847                else:
3848                    ntc_ref_df = ntc_df
3849                y_ntc_expr = ntc_ref_df['y_obs'] / ntc_ref_df['sum_factor']
3850                y_ntc_valid = y_ntc_expr[(y_ntc_expr > 0) & np.isfinite(y_ntc_expr)]
3851                if len(y_ntc_valid) == 0:  # fallback to pooled if reference group has no NTC
3852                    y_ntc_expr = ntc_df['y_obs'] / ntc_df['sum_factor']
3853                    y_ntc_valid = y_ntc_expr[(y_ntc_expr > 0) & np.isfinite(y_ntc_expr)]
3854                y_offset = np.log2(float(y_ntc_valid.mean())) if len(y_ntc_valid) > 0 else 0.0
3855    else:
3856        x_offset = 0.0
3857        y_offset = 0.0

3859    # Build color groups based on color_by.
3860    # color_by can be a str (single grouping) or a list of two str (cross-product).
3861    # Alpha_y correction is always per technical_group_code regardless of color_by.
3862
3863    def _resolve_grouping(cb):
3864        """Return list of (label, boolean_mask) for one color_by value, or None if not found."""
3865        if cb == 'technical_group':
3866            if 'technical_group_code' in df.columns:
3867                return [(code_to_label[int(gc)], df['technical_group_code'] == gc)
3868                        for gc in group_codes]
3869            return [('All', pd.Series(True, index=df.index))]
3870        if cb == 'targeting':
3871            ntc_m = df['target'].str.lower() == 'ntc'
3872            return [('NTC', ntc_m), ('Targeting', ~ntc_m)]
3873        if cb in df.columns:
3874            n_unique = df[cb].nunique()
3875            if n_unique == 0:
3876                warnings.warn(f"color_by='{cb}': column has no values after filtering.")
3877                return [('All', pd.Series(True, index=df.index))]
3878            if pd.api.types.is_float_dtype(df[cb]) and n_unique > 10:
3879                warnings.warn(
3880                    f"color_by='{cb}' looks continuous (float dtype, {n_unique} unique values). "
3881                    f"Coloring by a continuous column will produce many overlapping lines. "
3882                    f"Consider binning or using a categorical column instead."
3883                )
3884            elif n_unique > 30:
3885                warnings.warn(
3886                    f"color_by='{cb}' has {n_unique} unique values — this will produce "
3887                    f"{n_unique} smoothed lines and may be hard to read. "
3888                    f"Consider a coarser grouping."
3889                )
3890            uvals = sorted(df[cb].dropna().unique(), key=str)
3891            return [(str(v), df[cb] == v) for v in uvals]
3892        return None  # not found
3893
3894    _cb_list = [color_by] if isinstance(color_by, str) else list(color_by)
3895
3896    if len(_cb_list) == 1:
3897        # ── Single grouping ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
3898        groups = _resolve_grouping(_cb_list[0])
3899        if groups is None:
3900            warnings.warn(f"color_by='{_cb_list[0]}' not found in data; "
3901                          "falling back to 'technical_group'.")
3902            groups = _resolve_grouping('technical_group')
3903        color_groups_list = groups
3904
3905    else:
3906        # ── Cross-product of two groupings, with auto shade variation ────────
3907        # Primary grouping determines hue; secondary determines shade.
3908        # For 'targeting' as secondary: NTC → light shade, Targeting → full color.
3909        # For any other secondary: shades spread evenly from light to full.
3910        primary_cb, secondary_cb = _cb_list[0], _cb_list[1]
3911        primary_groups   = _resolve_grouping(primary_cb)   or _resolve_grouping('technical_group')
3912        secondary_groups = _resolve_grouping(secondary_cb) or [('All', pd.Series(True, index=df.index))]
3913
3914        if secondary_cb == 'targeting':
3915            _shade_for = {'NTC': 0.35, 'Targeting': 1.0}
3916        else:
3917            _n = len(secondary_groups)
3918            _shade_for = {lbl: 0.3 + 0.7 * i / max(_n - 1, 1)
3919                          for i, (lbl, _) in enumerate(secondary_groups)}
3920
3921        # Build cross-product; auto-populate color_palette with shade colours.
3922        # shade=1.0 → full base colour; shade<1.0 → mixed with white (lighter).
3923        from matplotlib.colors import to_rgb, to_hex
3924        color_palette = dict(color_palette)  # local copy — do not mutate caller's dict
3925        color_groups_list = []
3926        for pidx, (plabel, pmask) in enumerate(primary_groups):
3927            base_color = _color_for_label(plabel, fallback_idx=pidx, palette=color_palette)
3928            try:
3929                base_rgb = np.array(to_rgb(base_color))
3930            except ValueError:
3931                base_rgb = np.array([0.5, 0.5, 0.5])
3932            for slabel, smask in secondary_groups:
3933                combined_mask = pmask & smask
3934                if not combined_mask.any():
3935                    continue
3936                combined_label = f"{plabel} / {slabel}"
3937                if combined_label not in color_palette:
3938                    shade = _shade_for.get(slabel, 1.0)
3939                    shaded = np.clip(1 - shade * (1 - base_rgb), 0, 1)
3940                    color_palette[combined_label] = to_hex(shaded)
3941                color_groups_list.append((combined_label, combined_mask))
3942
3943    # Create colormaps for NTC gradient — one per color group (white → group color)
3944    group_cmaps = {}
3945    if show_ntc_gradient:
3946        for idx, (group_label, _) in enumerate(color_groups_list):
3947            base_color = _color_for_label(group_label, fallback_idx=idx, palette=color_palette)
3948            group_cmaps[group_label] = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(
3949                f"white_{group_label}", ["white", base_color]
3950            )
3951
3952    # Plot function
3953    def _plot_one(ax_plot, corrected):
3954        # Compute per-cell y_expr with alpha_y correction applied per technical group.
3955        # This is independent of color_by — correction always uses technical_group_code.
3956        if corrected and has_technical_fit:
3957            alpha_y_full = modality.alpha_y_prefit  # [C, T] or [S, C, T]
3958            y_expr_vals = np.empty(len(df))
3959            if 'technical_group_code' in df.columns:
3960                for gc in df['technical_group_code'].unique():
3961                    gc = int(gc)
3962                    if alpha_y_full.ndim == 3:
3963                        a = _to_scalar(alpha_y_full[:, gc, feature_idx].mean())
3964                    else:
3965                        a = _to_scalar(alpha_y_full[gc, feature_idx])
3966                    mask = df['technical_group_code'].values == gc
3967                    y_expr_vals[mask] = (df['y_obs'].values[mask] /
3968                                         (df['sum_factor'].values[mask] * a))
3969            else:
3970                y_expr_vals = (df['y_obs'] / df['sum_factor']).values
3971        else:
3972            y_expr_vals = (df['y_obs'] / df['sum_factor']).values
3973        y_expr_all = pd.Series(y_expr_vals, index=df.index)
3974
3975        # Accumulate bounds from plotted data so we can set explicit axis limits.
3976        # axhline / axvline are infinite lines that confuse matplotlib's auto-scaling;
3977        # explicit set_xlim / set_ylim ensures the view is driven by the data.
3978        _ax_x_segments = []   # (x_min, x_max) from each smooth curve
3979        _ax_y_segments = []   # (y_min, y_max) from each smooth curve
3980        _ax_y_hill = []       # y values from Hill curve (filtered to displayed x range)
3981        _ax_h_markers = []    # y positions of horizontal parameter lines
3982        _ax_v_markers = []    # x positions of vertical parameter lines (K / EC50)
3983
3984        colorbar_added = False
3985        for idx, (group_label, group_mask) in enumerate(color_groups_list):
3986            df_group = df[group_mask].copy()
3987            y_expr = y_expr_all[group_mask]
3988
3989            # Filter valid cells for kNN smoothing.
3990            # Require positive x_true (log2 axis) and finite y_expr.
3991            # Zero-count cells (y_expr=0) ARE included: isfinite(0) = True.
3992            # The Hill function is the model's *unconditional* expected value
3993            # E[y/SF] = A + α·Hill_a + β·Hill_b, which averages over all cells
3994            # including zero-count ones.  The y_offset (from mu_ntc or empirical NTC
3995            # mean) is also the unconditional reference.  Excluding zeros would raise
3996            # the kNN smooth to the *conditional* mean E[y/SF | y>0] > E[y/SF],
3997            # making it appear above the Hill curve.
3998            # Windows where every cell in the kNN neighbourhood has zero counts
3999            # are removed by the subsequent valid_smooth = y_smooth_linear > 0 filter,
4000            # so no log2(0) is ever taken.
4001            valid = (df_group['x_true'] > 0) & np.isfinite(y_expr)
4002            df_group = df_group[valid].copy()
4003            y_expr = y_expr[valid]
4004
4005            if len(df_group) == 0:
4006                continue
4007
4008            is_ntc_group = is_ntc[df_group.index].values
4009            k = _knn_k(len(df_group), window)
4010
4011            # k-NN smoothing in LINEAR space first (log2(mean(y)) ≥ mean(log2(y)))
4012            if show_ntc_gradient:
4013                x_smooth, y_smooth_linear, ntc_prop = _smooth_knn(
4014                    df_group['x_true'].values,
4015                    y_expr.values if hasattr(y_expr, 'values') else np.asarray(y_expr),
4016                    k, is_ntc=is_ntc_group
4017                )
4018                valid_smooth = y_smooth_linear > 0
4019                if not valid_smooth.all():
4020                    x_smooth = x_smooth[valid_smooth]
4021                    y_smooth_linear = y_smooth_linear[valid_smooth]
4022                    ntc_prop = ntc_prop[valid_smooth]
4023                y_smooth_log = np.log2(y_smooth_linear)
4024                _xs = np.log2(x_smooth) - x_offset
4025                _ys = y_smooth_log - y_offset
4026                group_cmap = group_cmaps.get(group_label, plt.cm.gray)
4027                plot_colored_line(
4028                    x=_xs, y=_ys,
4029                    color_values=1 - ntc_prop,
4030                    cmap=group_cmap, ax=ax_plot, linewidth=2
4031                )
4032                if len(_xs) > 0:
4033                    _ax_x_segments.append((float(_xs.min()), float(_xs.max())))
4034                    _ax_y_segments.append((float(_ys.min()), float(_ys.max())))
4035                color = _color_for_label(group_label, fallback_idx=idx, palette=color_palette)
4036                ax_plot.plot([], [], color=color, linewidth=2, label=group_label)
4037                if not colorbar_added:
4038                    fig = ax_plot.get_figure()
4039                    cmap_gray = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("gray_gradient", ["white", "black"])
4040                    sm = ScalarMappable(cmap=cmap_gray, norm=Normalize(0, 1))
4041                    sm.set_array([])
4042                    cbar = fig.colorbar(sm, ax=ax_plot)
4043                    cbar.set_label('1 - Proportion NTC (darker = fewer NTCs)')

4045            else:
4046                x_smooth, y_smooth_linear = _smooth_knn(
4047                    df_group['x_true'].values,
4048                    y_expr.values if hasattr(y_expr, 'values') else np.asarray(y_expr),
4049                    k
4050                )
4051                valid_smooth = y_smooth_linear > 0
4052                if not valid_smooth.all():
4053                    x_smooth = x_smooth[valid_smooth]
4054                    y_smooth_linear = y_smooth_linear[valid_smooth]
4055                y_smooth_log = np.log2(y_smooth_linear)
4056                _xs = np.log2(x_smooth) - x_offset
4057                _ys = y_smooth_log - y_offset
4058                color = _color_for_label(group_label, fallback_idx=idx, palette=color_palette)
4059                ax_plot.plot(_xs, _ys, color=color, linewidth=2, label=group_label)
4060                if len(_xs) > 0:
4061                    _ax_x_segments.append((float(_xs.min()), float(_xs.max())))
4062                    _ax_y_segments.append((float(_ys.min()), float(_ys.max())))
4063
4064        # Trans function overlay (if trans model fitted)
4065        # Show on corrected plot if available, otherwise show on uncorrected plot
4066        if show_hill_function and (corrected or not has_technical_fit):

4068            log2_min = np.log2(max(x_true.min(), 1e-6))
4069            log2_max = np.log2(x_true.max())
4070            if expand_x_to_params and mark_params:
4071                # Extend range to include K_a / K_b posterior means
4072                _posterior_ep = (model.posterior_samples_trans
4073                                 if modality.name == model.primary_modality
4074                                 else getattr(modality, 'posterior_samples_trans', None))
4075                if _posterior_ep is not None and 'K_a' in _posterior_ep:
4076                    _fnames_ep = (list(modality.feature_names)
4077                                  if modality.feature_names is not None else [])
4078                    if feature in _fnames_ep:

4080                        for _kname in ('K_a', 'K_b'):

4083                                _km = (_ks.mean(dim=0) if hasattr(_ks, 'mean')
4084                                       else np.mean(_ks, axis=0))
4085                                if hasattr(_km, 'detach'):

4087                                _km = np.asarray(_km).ravel()
4088                                if _fi_ep < len(_km):

4091                                        log2_min = min(log2_min, np.log2(_k_val))
4092                                        log2_max = max(log2_max, np.log2(_k_val))
4093            x_range = 2 ** np.linspace(log2_min, log2_max, 2000)

4097            _effective_fdr_df = fdr_df if fdr_df is not None else reference_df
4098            y_pred = predict_trans_function(model, feature, x_range, modality_name=None,
4099                                             fdr_threshold=fdr_threshold, fdr_df=_effective_fdr_df)
4100
4101            if y_pred is not None:
4102                # Transform prediction to log2(y) space to match data

4109                                color=hill_color, linestyle='--', linewidth=2,
4110                                label=hill_label)

4171                if _y_asym is not None:

4178            # Reference curve overlay (from trans_summary DataFrame)

4181                if _name_col:

4183                    if not _ref_match.empty:
4184                        _ref_row = _ref_match.iloc[0]
4185                        _x_ref = x_range if 'x_range' in dir() else (

4208                                    color=ref_color, linestyle='--', linewidth=2,
4209                                    alpha=0.8, label=ref_label)
4210                        # Reference mark_params: full set of Hill markers (A, Vmax, K)
4211                        if _show_ref_markers:
4212                            _ref_markers = _compute_hill_markers_from_summary_row(
4213                                _ref_row, log2_space=True, y_scale=1.0,
4214                                fdr_threshold=fdr_threshold,
4215                            )
4216                            # Reference markers use x_ntc/y_ntc as baselines (same as curve).
4217                            _y_ntc_ref_mk = float(_ref_row.get('y_ntc', 0.0)) if hasattr(_ref_row, 'get') else float(_ref_row['y_ntc'])
4218                            _x_ntc_ref_mk = float(_ref_row.get('x_ntc', 0.0)) if hasattr(_ref_row, 'get') else float(_ref_row['x_ntc'])
4219                            _y_ref_mk_offset = np.log2(_y_ntc_ref_mk) if (log2fc and _y_ntc_ref_mk > 0) else y_offset
4220                            _x_ref_mk_offset = np.log2(_x_ntc_ref_mk) if (log2fc and _x_ntc_ref_mk > 0) else x_offset
4221                            for _m in _ref_markers:
4222                                _kw = dict(linestyle=_m['linestyle'], color=ref_color,
4223                                           alpha=0.5, linewidth=1.2,
4224                                           label=f'Ref {_m["label"]}')
4225                                if _m['axis'] == 'h':
4226                                    ax_plot.axhline(_m['value'] - _y_ref_mk_offset, **_kw)
4227                                elif _m['axis'] == 'v':
4228                                    ax_plot.axvline(_m['value'] - _x_ref_mk_offset, **_kw)
4229
4230        ax_plot.set_xlabel("log2FC(x_true)" if log2fc else xlabel)
4231        ax_plot.set_ylabel(ylabel if ylabel is not None else ("log2FC(counts)" if log2fc else "log2(counts)"))
4232        title_suffix = ' (corrected)' if corrected else ' (uncorrected)'
4233        ax_plot.set_title(f"{model.cis_gene} → {feature}{title_suffix}")
4234        if log2fc:
4235            ax_plot.axhline(0, color='gray', linestyle=':', linewidth=0.8, alpha=0.6)
4236            ax_plot.axvline(0, color='gray', linestyle=':', linewidth=0.8, alpha=0.6)
4237
4238        # ── Explicit axis limits ──────────────────────────────────────────────
4239        # X: smooth data range, extended to include K/EC50 vertical markers.
4240        # Y: smooth data range + Hill curve (within displayed x range) + h markers.
4241        # axhline / axvline don't constrain auto-scaling reliably, so we set
4242        # limits manually to keep the view focused on the actual content.
4243        if _ax_x_segments:
4244            _x_lo = min(s[0] for s in _ax_x_segments)
4245            _x_hi = max(s[1] for s in _ax_x_segments)
4246            if _ax_v_markers:
4247                _x_lo = min(_x_lo, min(_ax_v_markers))
4248                _x_hi = max(_x_hi, max(_ax_v_markers))
4249
4250            _y_lo = min(s[0] for s in _ax_y_segments)
4251            _y_hi = max(s[1] for s in _ax_y_segments)
4252            if _ax_y_hill:
4253                _y_lo = min(_y_lo, min(_ax_y_hill))
4254                _y_hi = max(_y_hi, max(_ax_y_hill))
4255            if _ax_h_markers:
4256                _y_lo = min(_y_lo, min(_ax_h_markers))
4257                _y_hi = max(_y_hi, max(_ax_h_markers))
4258
4259            _x_pad = max(0.05 * (_x_hi - _x_lo), 0.1)
4260            _y_pad = max(0.05 * (_y_hi - _y_lo), 0.1)
4261            ax_plot.set_xlim(_x_lo - _x_pad, _x_hi + _x_pad)
4262            ax_plot.set_ylim(_y_lo - _y_pad, _y_hi + _y_pad)
4263
4264        if not legend_outside:
4265            ax_plot.legend(frameon=False)
4266
4267    # Plot
4268    if show_correction == 'both':
4269        _plot_one(axes[0], corrected=False)
4270        _plot_one(axes[1], corrected=True)
4271    elif show_correction == 'corrected':
4272        _plot_one(axes[0], corrected=True)
4273    else:
4274        _plot_one(axes[0], corrected=False)
4275
4276    if legend_outside:
4277        handles, labels = _collect_legend_handles(axes)
4278        axes[-1].legend(handles, labels, bbox_to_anchor=(1.03, 0.5), loc='center left', frameon=False)
4279
4280    return axes[0] if len(axes) == 1 else axes

Plot negbinom (gene counts) with optional Hill function overlay.

Y-axis: log2(counts / sum_factor), optionally alpha_y-corrected.

Parameters (selected)

color_by : str or list of two str What to color smoothed lines by. Options: - 'technical_group' (default): one line per cell-line / technical group - 'targeting': two lines — NTC vs all targeting cells - Any column name in model.meta: one line per unique value - A list of two values (e.g. ['technical_group', 'targeting']): cross-product of two groupings. The first determines hue; the second determines shade — NTC gets a lighter tint of the group colour, Targeting gets the full colour.

Parameters
  • show_ntc_gradient (bool): If True, color lines by NTC proportion in k-NN window (default: False) Lighter colors = more NTC cells, Darker colors = fewer NTC cells Only applies to uncorrected plots
  • sum_factor_col (str): Column name in model.meta for sum factors (default: 'sum_factor') Can be 'sum_factor', 'sum_factor_adj', or any other sum factor column
  • min_counts (int): Minimum raw counts to include a cell (default: 0, i.e., include all cells)
def plot_binomial_xy( model, feature: str, modality, x_true: numpy.ndarray, window: int, min_counts: int, color_palette: Dict[str, str], show_trans_function: bool, show_ntc_gradient: bool = False, show_correction: str = 'both', xlabel: str = 'log2(x_true)', ax: Optional[matplotlib.axes._axes.Axes] = None, subset_mask: Optional[numpy.ndarray] = None, mark_params=False, ci_level: float = 95.0, legend_outside: bool = False, figsize: Optional[Tuple[float, float]] = None, log2fc: bool = False, ntc_x_offset: Optional[float] = None, ylabel: Optional[str] = None, **kwargs) -> matplotlib.axes._axes.Axes: 
4283def plot_binomial_xy(
4284    model,
4285    feature: str,
4286    modality,
4287    x_true: np.ndarray,
4288    window: int,
4289    min_counts: int,
4290    color_palette: Dict[str, str],
4291    show_trans_function: bool,
4292    show_ntc_gradient: bool = False,
4293    show_correction: str = 'both',
4294    xlabel: str = "log2(x_true)",
4295    ax: Optional[plt.Axes] = None,
4296    subset_mask: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
4297    mark_params = False,
4298    ci_level: float = 95.0,
4299    legend_outside: bool = False,
4300    figsize: Optional[Tuple[float, float]] = None,
4301    log2fc: bool = False,
4302    ntc_x_offset: Optional[float] = None,
4303    ylabel: Optional[str] = None,
4304    **kwargs
4305) -> plt.Axes:
4306    """
4307    Plot binomial (a bounded count/denominator ratio, e.g. PSI or a
4308    spliced/unspliced fraction).
4309
4310    Y-axis: 100 * counts / denominator (percentage scale: 0-100). Labeled
4311    ``'Percentage (%)'`` by default since this distribution is used for any
4312    bounded count/denominator ratio, not just splicing PSI (e.g. gene-level
4313    spliced-vs-unspliced fractions for velocity) -- pass ``ylabel='PSI (%)'``
4314    (or another description) to be more specific for a given modality.
4315    Filter: min_counts on denominator
4316
4317    Parameters
4318    ----------
4319    show_ntc_gradient : bool
4320        If True, color lines by NTC proportion in k-NN window (default: False)
4321        Lighter colors = more NTC cells, Darker colors = fewer NTC cells
4322    show_correction : str
4323        'uncorrected': no technical correction
4324        'corrected': apply alpha_y_add additive correction (PSI - alpha_y_add)
4325        'both': show both side-by-side
4326    log2fc : bool
4327        If True, x-axis becomes log2(x_true) - log2(mean NTC x_true) (log2FC
4328        relative to NTC) instead of raw log2(x_true). The y-axis (PSI%) is left
4329        as-is -- unlike negbinom, there is no natural log2FC transform for a
4330        bounded proportion, so only the x-axis shifts. A grey dotted vertical
4331        line is drawn at x=0 to mark the NTC reference.
4332    ntc_x_offset : float, optional
4333        Precomputed log2(mean NTC x_true) offset (see ``_compute_global_log2fc_offsets``).
4334        Required for ``log2fc=True`` to have any effect; ``plot_xy_data`` computes
4335        and passes this automatically.
4336    ylabel : str, optional
4337        Override the y-axis label (default: ``'Percentage (%)'``). Pass
4338        ``ylabel='PSI (%)'`` for splicing modalities, or e.g.
4339        ``ylabel='Spliced (%)'`` for a gene velocity modality.
4340
4341    Notes
4342    -----
4343    Technical correction for binomial uses alpha_y_add (additive correction on LOGIT scale).
4344    logit(PSI) = log(PSI / (1 - PSI))
4345    logit_corrected = logit(PSI) - alpha_y_add
4346    PSI_corrected = 1 / (1 + exp(-logit_corrected))
4347    """
4348    _x_off = ntc_x_offset if (log2fc and ntc_x_offset is not None) else 0.0
4349    # Get data
4350    feature_idx = _get_feature_index(feature, modality)
4351    if feature_idx is None:
4352        raise ValueError(f"Feature '{feature}' not found in modality")
4353
4354    # Get counts and denominator
4355    if modality.cells_axis == 1:
4356        counts = modality.counts[feature_idx, :]
4357        denom = modality.denominator[feature_idx, :]
4358    else:
4359        counts = modality.counts[:, feature_idx]
4360        denom = modality.denominator[:, feature_idx]
4361
4362    # Align cells between model.meta and modality
4363    x_true_aligned, counts_aligned, meta_aligned = _align_cells_to_modality(
4364        model, modality, x_true, counts, subset_mask
4365    )
4366    # Also align denominator (same cell alignment)
4367    _, denom_aligned, _ = _align_cells_to_modality(
4368        model, modality, x_true, denom, subset_mask
4369    )
4370
4371    # Filter by min_counts
4372    valid_mask = denom_aligned >= min_counts
4373
4374    # Build dataframe
4375    df_data = {
4376        'x_true': x_true_aligned[valid_mask],
4377        'counts': counts_aligned[valid_mask],
4378        'denominator': denom_aligned[valid_mask],
4379        'target': meta_aligned['target'].values[valid_mask]
4380    }
4381
4382    # Conditionally add technical_group_code if it exists
4383    if 'technical_group_code' in meta_aligned.columns:
4384        df_data['technical_group_code'] = meta_aligned['technical_group_code'].values[valid_mask]
4385
4386    df = pd.DataFrame(df_data)
4387
4388    # Keep counts and denominators for binning (don't compute PSI per-cell)
4389    # Filter valid
4390    valid = (df['x_true'] > 0) & (df['denominator'] > 0)
4391    df = df[valid].copy()
4392
4393    if len(df) == 0:
4394        raise ValueError(f"No data remaining after filtering (min_counts={min_counts})")
4395
4396    # Check technical correction availability
4397    # First check attribute, then fall back to posterior_samples_ntc dict
4398    has_technical_fit = False
4399    if hasattr(modality, 'alpha_y_prefit_add') and modality.alpha_y_prefit_add is not None:
4400        has_technical_fit = True
4401    elif hasattr(modality, 'posterior_samples_ntc') and modality.posterior_samples_ntc is not None:
4402        if 'alpha_y_add' in modality.posterior_samples_ntc:
4403            has_technical_fit = True
4404            # Set the attribute for future use
4405            modality.alpha_y_prefit_add = modality.posterior_samples_ntc['alpha_y_add']
4406            print(f"[INFO] Set alpha_y_prefit_add from posterior_samples_ntc for modality '{modality.name}'")
4407
4408    if show_correction == 'corrected' and not has_technical_fit:
4409        warnings.warn(f"Technical fit not available for modality '{modality.name}' - showing uncorrected only")
4410        show_correction = 'uncorrected'
4411
4412    # Create axes
4413    if ax is None:
4414        if show_correction == 'both':
4415            fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=figsize or (14, 5))
4416        else:
4417            fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 1, figsize=figsize or (8, 5))
4418            axes = [ax]
4419    else:
4420        # Single axis provided - in multifeature mode, function is called twice
4421        # (once with 'uncorrected' and once with 'corrected'), so don't override show_correction
4422        axes = [ax]
4423
4424    # Get technical group labels
4425    code_to_label = _labels_by_code_for_df(model, df)
4426
4427    if 'technical_group_code' in df.columns:
4428        group_codes = np.sort(df['technical_group_code'].unique())
4429    else:
4430        group_codes = np.array([0])  # Single group
4431
4432    group_labels = [code_to_label[int(c)] for c in group_codes]
4433
4434    # Detect NTC cells for gradient coloring
4435    is_ntc = df['target'].str.lower() == 'ntc'
4436
4437    # Create colormaps for NTC gradient (per technical group)
4438    # Each group gets white → group_color gradient
4439    group_cmaps = {}
4440    if show_ntc_gradient:
4441        for group_label in group_labels:
4442            base_color = color_palette.get(group_label, f'C0')
4443            # Create colormap: white (low color value) → group color (high color value)
4444            group_cmaps[group_label] = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(
4445                f"white_{group_label}",
4446                ["white", base_color]
4447            )
4448
4449    # Plot function
4450    def _plot_one(ax_plot, corrected):
4451        colorbar_added = False  # Track if colorbar added
4452        
4453        for idx, group_code in enumerate(group_codes):
4454            group_code = int(group_code)
4455            group_label = code_to_label[group_code]
4456            color = _color_for_label(group_label, fallback_idx=idx, palette=color_palette)
4457
4458            # Get data for this group
4459            if 'technical_group_code' in df.columns:
4460                group_mask = df['technical_group_code'] == group_code
4461            else:
4462                group_mask = pd.Series([True] * len(df), index=df.index)
4463
4464            if group_mask.sum() == 0:
4465                continue
4466
4467            x_group = df.loc[group_mask, 'x_true'].values
4468            counts_group = df.loc[group_mask, 'counts'].values       # (n_cells_group,)
4469            denom_group = df.loc[group_mask, 'denominator'].values   # (n_cells_group,)
4470
4471            # Bin counts using k-NN
4472            k = _knn_k(len(x_group), window)
4473            x_smooth, counts_binned, denom_binned = _smooth_knn_counts(
4474                x_group, counts_group, denom_group, k
4475            )  # counts_binned: (n_bins,), denom_binned: (n_bins,)
4476
4477            # Compute PSI from binned counts (as proportion [0, 1])
4478            epsilon = 1e-10
4479            with np.errstate(divide='ignore', invalid='ignore'):
4480                p_binned = np.where(denom_binned > epsilon,
4481                                    counts_binned / denom_binned,
4482                                    0.5)  # Default to 0.5 if no data
4483
4484            if corrected and has_technical_fit:
4485                # Apply additive correction on LOGIT scale to binned proportions
4486                # 1. Clip proportions to avoid log(0) or log(1)
4487                epsilon_clip = 1e-6
4488                p_clipped = np.clip(p_binned, epsilon_clip, 1 - epsilon_clip)
4489
4490                # 2. Calculate logit
4491                logit_p = np.log(p_clipped / (1 - p_clipped))
4492
4493                # 3. Apply correction on logit scale
4494                alpha_y_add = modality.alpha_y_prefit_add
4495                if alpha_y_add.ndim == 3:
4496                    correction = _to_scalar(alpha_y_add[:, group_code, feature_idx].mean())
4497                else:
4498                    correction = _to_scalar(alpha_y_add[group_code, feature_idx])
4499                logit_corrected = logit_p - correction
4500
4501                # 4. Convert back to proportion
4502                p_corrected = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-logit_corrected))
4503
4504                # 5. Convert to percentage
4505                y_smooth = p_corrected * 100.0
4506            else:
4507                # Convert uncorrected proportion to percentage
4508                y_smooth = p_binned * 100.0
4509
4510            # Plot (no additional smoothing needed - already binned)
4511            # Note: We don't currently support NTC gradient for binned data
4512            ax_plot.plot(np.log2(x_smooth) - _x_off, y_smooth, color=color, linewidth=2, label=group_label)
4513
4514        # Trans function overlay (if trans model fitted)
4515        # Show on corrected plot if available, otherwise show on uncorrected plot
4516        if show_trans_function and (corrected or not has_technical_fit):
4517            # Evenly spaced points in log2 space for smooth curve on log-log plot
4518            log2_min = np.log2(max(x_true.min(), 1e-6))
4519            log2_max = np.log2(x_true.max())
4520            x_range = 2 ** np.linspace(log2_min, log2_max, 2000)
4521            y_pred = predict_trans_function(model, feature, x_range, modality_name=modality.name)
4522
4523            if y_pred is not None:
4524                # For binomial, PSI is in percentage scale [0, 100], so scale and clip predictions
4525                y_pred_pct = y_pred * 100.0
4526                y_pred_clipped = np.clip(y_pred_pct, 0, 100)
4527                ax_plot.plot(np.log2(x_range) - _x_off, y_pred_clipped,
4528                           color='black', linestyle='--', linewidth=2,
4529                           label='Fitted Trans Function')
4530
4531        # Full parameter markers (PSI%, linear y-axis)
4532        if mark_params and (corrected or not has_technical_fit):
4533            _markers = _compute_hill_markers(
4534                model, feature, modality,
4535                log2_space=False, y_scale=100.0
4536            )
4537            _draw_hill_markers(ax_plot, _markers, x_offset=_x_off)
4538
4539        ax_plot.set_xlabel("log2FC(x_true)" if log2fc else xlabel)
4540        ax_plot.set_ylabel(ylabel if ylabel is not None else 'Percentage (%)')
4541        title_suffix = ' (corrected)' if corrected else ' (uncorrected)'
4542        ax_plot.set_title(f"{model.cis_gene} → {feature} (min_counts={min_counts}{title_suffix})")
4543        if log2fc:
4544            ax_plot.axvline(0, color='gray', linestyle=':', linewidth=0.8, alpha=0.6)
4545        if not legend_outside:
4546            ax_plot.legend(frameon=False)
4547
4548    # Plot
4549    # NOTE: When ax is provided (multifeature mode), show_correction will be 'uncorrected' or 'corrected'
4550    # (forced by warning above), so we respect the show_correction value
4551    if show_correction == 'both':
4552        _plot_one(axes[0], corrected=False)
4553        _plot_one(axes[1], corrected=True)
4554    elif show_correction == 'corrected':
4555        _plot_one(axes[0], corrected=True)
4556    else:  # show_correction == 'uncorrected'
4557        _plot_one(axes[0], corrected=False)
4558
4559    if legend_outside:
4560        handles, labels = _collect_legend_handles(axes)
4561        axes[-1].legend(handles, labels, bbox_to_anchor=(1.03, 0.5), loc='center left', frameon=False)
4562
4563    return axes[0] if len(axes) == 1 else axes

Plot binomial (a bounded count/denominator ratio, e.g. PSI or a spliced/unspliced fraction).

Y-axis: 100 * counts / denominator (percentage scale: 0-100). Labeled 'Percentage (%)' by default since this distribution is used for any bounded count/denominator ratio, not just splicing PSI (e.g. gene-level spliced-vs-unspliced fractions for velocity) -- pass ylabel='PSI (%)' (or another description) to be more specific for a given modality. Filter: min_counts on denominator

Parameters
  • show_ntc_gradient (bool): If True, color lines by NTC proportion in k-NN window (default: False) Lighter colors = more NTC cells, Darker colors = fewer NTC cells
  • show_correction (str): 'uncorrected': no technical correction 'corrected': apply alpha_y_add additive correction (PSI - alpha_y_add) 'both': show both side-by-side
  • log2fc (bool): If True, x-axis becomes log2(x_true) - log2(mean NTC x_true) (log2FC relative to NTC) instead of raw log2(x_true). The y-axis (PSI%) is left as-is -- unlike negbinom, there is no natural log2FC transform for a bounded proportion, so only the x-axis shifts. A grey dotted vertical line is drawn at x=0 to mark the NTC reference.
  • ntc_x_offset (float, optional): Precomputed log2(mean NTC x_true) offset (see _compute_global_log2fc_offsets). Required for log2fc=True to have any effect; plot_xy_data computes and passes this automatically.
  • ylabel (str, optional): Override the y-axis label (default: 'Percentage (%)'). Pass ylabel='PSI (%)' for splicing modalities, or e.g. ylabel='Spliced (%)' for a gene velocity modality.
Notes

Technical correction for binomial uses alpha_y_add (additive correction on LOGIT scale). logit(PSI) = log(PSI / (1 - PSI)) logit_corrected = logit(PSI) - alpha_y_add PSI_corrected = 1 / (1 + exp(-logit_corrected))

def plot_multinomial_xy( model, feature: str, modality, x_true: numpy.ndarray, window: int, min_counts: int, show_correction: str, color_palette: Dict[str, str], show_trans_function: bool, show_ntc_gradient: bool = False, xlabel: str = 'log2(x_true)', figsize: Optional[Tuple[int, int]] = None, subset_mask: Optional[numpy.ndarray] = None, log2fc: bool = False, ntc_x_offset: Optional[float] = None, ylabel: Optional[str] = None, **kwargs) -> Union[matplotlib.figure.Figure, List[matplotlib.axes._axes.Axes]]: 
4566def plot_multinomial_xy(
4567    model,
4568    feature: str,
4569    modality,
4570    x_true: np.ndarray,
4571    window: int,
4572    min_counts: int,
4573    show_correction: str,
4574    color_palette: Dict[str, str],
4575    show_trans_function: bool,
4576    show_ntc_gradient: bool = False,
4577    xlabel: str = "log2(x_true)",
4578    figsize: Optional[Tuple[int, int]] = None,
4579    subset_mask: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
4580    log2fc: bool = False,
4581    ntc_x_offset: Optional[float] = None,
4582    ylabel: Optional[str] = None,
4583    **kwargs
4584) -> Union[plt.Figure, List[plt.Axes]]:
4585    """
4586    Plot multinomial (e.g., donor/acceptor usage) - one subplot per category.
4587
4588    Y-axis: Proportion for each category
4589    Layout:
4590    - If show_correction='uncorrected' or 'corrected': K columns (one per category), 1 row
4591    - If show_correction='both': 2 columns (uncorrected left, corrected right), K rows (one per category)
4592
4593    Parameters
4594    ----------
4595    show_ntc_gradient : bool
4596        If True, color lines by NTC proportion in k-NN window (default: False)
4597        **Note**: Not yet fully implemented for multinomial - will issue warning
4598    log2fc : bool
4599        If True, x-axis becomes log2(x_true) - log2(mean NTC x_true) (log2FC
4600        relative to NTC) instead of raw log2(x_true). The y-axis (proportion) is
4601        left as-is. A grey dotted vertical line is drawn at x=0 (NTC reference).
4602    ntc_x_offset : float, optional
4603        Precomputed log2(mean NTC x_true) offset (see ``_compute_global_log2fc_offsets``).
4604        Required for ``log2fc=True`` to have any effect; ``plot_xy_data`` computes
4605        and passes this automatically.
4606
4607    Notes
4608    -----
4609    Technical correction for multinomial uses alpha_y_add (additive on LOGIT scale).
4610    logits_corrected = logits - alpha_y_add
4611    proportions_corrected = softmax(logits_corrected)
4612    """
4613    _x_off = ntc_x_offset if (log2fc and ntc_x_offset is not None) else 0.0
4614    if show_ntc_gradient:
4615        warnings.warn("NTC gradient coloring not yet implemented for multinomial distributions - using standard colors")
4616
4617    # Get data
4618    feature_idx = _get_feature_index(feature, modality)
4619    if feature_idx is None:
4620        raise ValueError(f"Feature '{feature}' not found in modality")
4621
4622    # Get counts: shape (cells, K) for this feature
4623    if modality.counts.ndim == 3:
4624        counts_3d = modality.counts[feature_idx, :, :]  # (cells, K)
4625    else:
4626        raise ValueError(f"Expected 3D counts for multinomial, got {modality.counts.ndim}D")
4627
4628    K = counts_3d.shape[1]
4629

Plot multinomial (e.g., donor/acceptor usage) - one subplot per category.

Y-axis: Proportion for each category Layout:

  • If show_correction='uncorrected' or 'corrected': K columns (one per category), 1 row
  • If show_correction='both': 2 columns (uncorrected left, corrected right), K rows (one per category)
Parameters
  • show_ntc_gradient (bool): If True, color lines by NTC proportion in k-NN window (default: False) Note: Not yet fully implemented for multinomial - will issue warning
  • log2fc (bool): If True, x-axis becomes log2(x_true) - log2(mean NTC x_true) (log2FC relative to NTC) instead of raw log2(x_true). The y-axis (proportion) is left as-is. A grey dotted vertical line is drawn at x=0 (NTC reference).
  • ntc_x_offset (float, optional): Precomputed log2(mean NTC x_true) offset (see _compute_global_log2fc_offsets). Required for log2fc=True to have any effect; plot_xy_data computes and passes this automatically.
Notes

Technical correction for multinomial uses alpha_y_add (additive on LOGIT scale). logits_corrected = logits - alpha_y_add proportions_corrected = softmax(logits_corrected)

4926    ntc_x_offset : float, optional

4931    _x_off = ntc_x_offset if (log2fc and ntc_x_offset is not None) else 0.0
4932    # Get data

4947
4948    # Build dataframe

4951        'y_val': y_vals_aligned,
4952        'target': meta_aligned['target'].values
4953    }
4954
4955    # Conditionally add technical_group_code if it exists

4958
4959    df = pd.DataFrame(df_data)
4960
4961    # Filter valid
4962    valid = (df['x_true'] > 0) & np.isfinite(df['y_val'])

4964
4965    # Check technical correction

4971        if 'alpha_y_add' in modality.posterior_samples_ntc:

5106                log2_space=False, y_scale=1.0
5107            )
5108            _draw_hill_markers(ax_plot, _markers, x_offset=_x_off)
5109
5110        ax_plot.set_xlabel("log2FC(x_true)" if log2fc else xlabel)
5111        ax_plot.set_ylabel(ylabel if ylabel is not None else 'Value')
5112        title_suffix = ' (corrected)' if corrected else ' (uncorrected)'
5113        ax_plot.set_title(f"{model.cis_gene} → {feature}{title_suffix}")
5114        if log2fc:
5115            ax_plot.axvline(0, color='gray', linestyle=':', linewidth=0.8, alpha=0.6)
5116        if not legend_outside:
5117            ax_plot.legend(frameon=False)
5118
5119    # Plot
5120    if show_correction == 'both':
5121        _plot_one(axes[0], corrected=False)
5122        _plot_one(axes[1], corrected=True)
5123    elif show_correction == 'corrected':
5124        _plot_one(axes[0], corrected=True)
5125    else:
5126        _plot_one(axes[0], corrected=False)
5127
5128    if legend_outside:
5129        handles, labels = _collect_legend_handles(axes)
5130        axes[-1].legend(handles, labels, bbox_to_anchor=(1.03, 0.5), loc='center left', frameon=False)
5131
5132    return axes[0] if len(axes) == 1 else axes

Plot normal or studentT distribution (continuous scores like SpliZ).

Y-axis: Raw value

Parameters
  • show_ntc_gradient (bool): If True, color lines by NTC proportion in k-NN window (default: False) Lighter colors = more NTC cells, Darker colors = fewer NTC cells Only applies to uncorrected plots

  • ntc_x_offset (float, optional): Precomputed log2(mean NTC x_true) offset (see _compute_global_log2fc_offsets). Required for log2fc=True to have any effect; plot_xy_data computes and passes this automatically.

5508    model,
5509    feature: str,
5510    modality_name: Optional[str] = None,
