5538) -> Union[plt.Figure, plt.Axes]:
5539    """
5540    Plot raw x-y data showing relationship between cis gene expression and modality values.
5541
5542    Requires x_true to be set (must run fit_cis() first).
5543
5544    Parameters
5545    ----------
5546    model : bayesDREAM
5547        Fitted bayesDREAM model with x_true set
5548    feature : str
5549        Feature name (junction, donor, etc.) OR gene name.
5550        - If a specific feature name (e.g., 'chr1:999788:999865'), plots that feature
5551        - If a gene name (e.g., 'HES4'), plots all features for that gene in subplots
5552        - Requires modality to have gene information ('gene', 'gene_name', or 'gene_id' columns)
5553    modality_name : str, optional
5554        Modality name (default: primary modality)
5555    window : int
5556        k-NN window size for smoothing (default: 100 cells)
5557    show_correction : str
5558        'uncorrected': no technical correction
5559        'corrected': apply alpha_y technical correction
5560        'both': show both side-by-side (default)
5561    min_counts : int, optional
5562        Minimum raw counts to include cells.
5563        Default depends on distribution: 0 for negbinom, 3 for binomial/multinomial.
5564        For negbinom: excludes cells with y_obs < min_counts
5565        For binomial: minimum denominator
5566        For multinomial: minimum total counts
5567    color_palette : dict, optional
5568        Custom colors for technical groups, keyed by the group label string
5569        Example: {'K562': 'crimson', 'TF1': 'dodgerblue'}
5570    show_hill_function : bool
5571        Overlay fitted trans function if trans model fitted (all distributions, default: True)
5572        Works with all function types: additive_hill, single_hill, polynomial
5573        Automatically detects function type from posterior_samples_trans
5574    show_ntc_gradient : bool
5575        Color lines by NTC proportion in k-NN window (default: False)
5576        Lighter colors = more NTC cells, Darker colors = fewer NTC cells
5577        Only applies to uncorrected plots
5578        Fully implemented for: negbinom, binomial, normal, studentt
5579        Not yet implemented for: multinomial (will issue warning)
5580    sum_factor_col : str
5581        Column name in model.meta for sum factors (default: 'sum_factor')
5582        Can be 'sum_factor', 'sum_factor_adj', or any other sum factor column
5583        Only used for negbinom distribution (gene expression)
5584    xlabel : str
5585        X-axis label (default: "log2(x_true)")
5586    ylabel : str, optional
5587        Override the y-axis label (default: None, uses a distribution-specific
5588        default -- ``"log2(counts)"`` for negbinom, ``"Percentage (%)"`` for
5589        binomial (0-100 scale), ``"Proportion"`` for multinomial (0-1 scale),
5590        ``"Value"`` for normal/studentt). The binomial default is deliberately
5591        generic since that distribution covers any bounded count/denominator
5592        ratio, not just splicing PSI -- pass e.g. ``ylabel='PSI (%)'`` for
5593        splicing modalities or ``ylabel='Spliced (%)'`` for a gene velocity
5594        modality.
5595    figsize : tuple, optional
5596        Figure size (auto-sized if None)
5597    src_barcodes : np.ndarray, optional
5598        Source barcode order if x_true not in model.meta order
5599    subset_meta : dict, optional
5600        Subset cells by metadata columns. Dictionary of {column: value} pairs.
5601        Example: {'target': 'ntc'} - plot only NTC cells
5602        Example: {'cell_line': 'K562'} - plot only K562 cells
5603        Example: {'lane': 'L1', 'cell_line': 'K562'} - plot L1 lane K562 cells
5604        Multiple conditions are combined with AND logic.
5605    exclude_cells : list of str, optional
5606        Cell names (matched against ``model.meta['cell']``) to drop before
5607        plotting, e.g. cells identified by ``check_systematic_shift``'s
5608        ``exclude_cells`` filtering logic. AND-combined with ``subset_meta``
5609        when both are given, without needing to call ``model.subset_cells()``
5610        first.
5611        Example: ``exclude_cells=['cell_1', 'cell_2']``
5612    only_dependent : bool
5613        If True and plotting multiple features (gene name), filter to only "dependent" features
5614        (default: False). When ``fdr_df`` is provided, uses its precomputed ``is_dependent``
5615        column (FDR-significant AND the Hill coefficient's credible interval excludes 0).
5616        Otherwise falls back to filtering on the n_a/n_b credible interval alone, which
5617        requires fit_trans() to have been run with function_type='additive_hill'.
5618        Ignored for single-feature plots.
5619    ci_level : float
5620        Credible interval level for dependency filtering and parameter marker
5621        classification (default: 95.0).
5622        Used by only_dependent=True and mark_params=True.
5623    mark_params : bool or str
5624        Overlay meaningful parameter markers on the Hill function (default: False).
5625        Requires show_hill_function=True and fit_trans() completed with
5626        function_type='single_hill' or 'additive_hill'.
5627        - True or 'both': markers for both the fitted curve and the reference curve
5628        - 'fit': markers for the fitted curve only
5629        - 'reference': markers for the reference curve only (requires reference_df)
5630        - False or None: no markers
5631        Markers drawn depend on the fitted regime:
5632        - **Single Hill / effectively single**: log2(A), log2(A+α·Vmax), log2(EC50)
5633        - **Same-sign additive** (both Hills in same direction):
5634          log2(A), log2(A+α·Vmax_a+β·Vmax_b), log2(EC50_lower), log2(EC50_upper)
5635        - **Non-monotonic** (opposite-sign Hills):
5636          log2(y: x→0), log2(y: x→∞), log2(EC50_lower), log2(EC50_upper);
5637          additionally log2(A+α·Vmax_a+β·Vmax_b) [peak] if activation EC50 < inhibition EC50
5638        For non-negbinom distributions, all y-axis markers are in linear space.
5639        Note: asymptotes include the α/β weight factors (e.g. A+α·Vmax, not A+Vmax).
5640    log2fc : bool
5641        If True, x-axis becomes log2(x_true) - log2(mean NTC x_true) (log2FC
5642        relative to NTC) instead of raw log2(x_true) (default: False).
5643        For **negbinom**, the y-axis also becomes log2FC relative to NTC
5644        (log2(counts) - log2(mean NTC counts, reference group)), and a grey
5645        dotted crosshair is drawn at (0, 0).
5646        For **binomial/normal/studentt/multinomial**, only the x-axis
5647        transforms -- the y-axis is left in its natural scale (PSI%, raw
5648        value, proportion), since there's no natural log2FC transform for a
5649        bounded/non-count quantity. Only a vertical grey dotted line is drawn
5650        at x=0 to mark the NTC reference.
5651    color_by : str or list of two str
5652        What to color smoothed lines by (default: ``'technical_group'``).
5653        - ``'technical_group'``: one line per cell-line / technical group (default)
5654        - ``'targeting'``: two lines — ``NTC`` vs ``Targeting``
5655        - **Any column name in ``model.meta``**: one line per unique value.
5656          A warning is issued if the column looks continuous (float dtype with many
5657          unique values) or has more than 30 unique values.
5658        - **List of two** (e.g. ``['technical_group', 'targeting']``): cross-product of
5659          two groupings — the first sets hue, the second sets shade. When the secondary
5660          is ``'targeting'``, NTC lines are drawn as a light tint of the group colour
5661          and targeting lines as the full colour (matching the classic "shades" style).
5662          Override any auto-generated colour via ``color_palette`` using the combined
5663          label ``"K562 / NTC"``, ``"K562 / Targeting"``, etc.
5664        Alpha-y technical correction is always applied per technical group regardless
5665        of this setting.
5666    facet_by : str or list of str, optional
5667        Column name(s) to facet by (default: ``None``).  Accepts either a
5668        single string or a list of **at most two** strings.  Each value may be
5669        a real column name in ``model.meta`` **or** one of the same special
5670        keywords supported by ``color_by``:
5671
5672        - ``'targeting'`` — two panels: ``NTC`` / ``Targeting``
5673          (derived from ``model.meta['target']``)
5674        - ``'technical_group'`` — one panel per technical group code
5675
5676        Analogous to ``facet_grid`` in ggplot2.
5677
5678        **1 column** (``facet_by='cell_line'``) — all unique values become
5679        side-by-side column groups::
5680
5681            rows = n_features,  cols = n_facets × n_corrections
5682
5683        Example: 3 cell lines + ``show_correction='both'`` →  1 × 6 grid
5684        ``[K562 uncorr | K562 corr | TF1 uncorr | TF1 corr | HL60 uncorr | HL60 corr]``
5685
5686        **2 columns** (``facet_by=['cell_line', 'perturbation']``) — first
5687        column maps to grid *rows*, second column maps to grid *columns*::
5688
5689            rows = n_facet1_values × n_features
5690            cols = n_facet2_values × n_corrections
5691
5692        Example: 3 cell lines × 2 perturbation types + ``show_correction='corrected'``
5693        → 3 × 2 grid (cell lines as rows, perturbation types as columns).
5694
5695        **Combining with other parameters:**
5696
5697        - ``subset_meta`` / ``exclude_cells``: each facet mask is AND-combined
5698          with the global ``subset_meta`` / ``exclude_cells`` filters, so you
5699          can first narrow to CRISPRi cells (or drop specific cells) and then
5700          facet by cell line within that subset.
5701        - ``color_by``: works independently within each panel — e.g.
5702          ``facet_by='cell_line'`` splits cell lines into columns while
5703          ``color_by='targeting'`` still draws NTC / Targeting lines *inside*
5704          each panel.
5705        - ``legend_outside=True``: recommended when faceting produces many
5706          panels, to keep the shared legend out of the plot area.
5707
5708        Facet labels appear as the first line of each panel title, e.g.
5709        ``cell_line=K562`` or ``cell_line=K562  perturbation=CRISPRi``.
5710        A warning is issued for columns with more than 20 unique values.
5711        Not yet supported for ``multinomial`` distributions (ignored with a
5712        warning in that case).
5713    expand_x_to_params : bool
5714        When True, extend the x-axis (and the Hill curve) beyond the data range
5715        so that all K/EC50 parameters are visible on the plot (default: False).
5716        Requires ``show_hill_function=True`` and a fitted trans model.
5717        The x-axis minimum and maximum are widened to include the mean K_a and
5718        K_b values from the posterior, so any EC50 that falls outside the data
5719        range will still appear on the curve.  Ignored for polynomial function
5720        types (which have no K parameters).
5721    expand_y_to_params : bool
5722        When True, extend the y-axis to show the full range of the fitted Hill
5723        curve over the entire displayed x range, including any x values added by
5724        ``expand_x_to_params`` (default: False).  Normally the Hill curve's y
5725        values are only used for y-axis scaling within the data x range; this
5726        flag removes that restriction so the y-axis accommodates the Hill
5727        curve's y values at K/EC50 positions and at the asymptotes.
5728    legend_outside : bool
5729        Place the legend outside the panel to the right, shared across all panels
5730        (default: False). Useful when many lines clutter the plot area.
5731    filename : str, optional
5732        If provided, save the figure to ``model.output_dir / filename``.
5733        A ``.png`` extension is added automatically if none is given.
5734        Use a full path to save elsewhere.
5735    figsize : tuple, optional
5736        Figure size as ``(width, height)`` in inches.  When None (default) the
5737        size is chosen automatically: 6 inches per column × 3 inches per row
5738        for multi-panel plots, or (8, 5) / (14, 5) for single-panel plots.
5739    reference_df : pd.DataFrame, optional
5740        A ``trans_summary`` DataFrame whose rows contain fitted Hill parameters
5741        (columns ending in ``_median``, e.g. ``A_median``, ``Vmax_a_median``, etc.).
5742        When provided, a reference Hill curve is overlaid in red dashed on each
5743        negbinom panel.  The feature name is matched via a ``gene_name`` or
5744        ``gene`` column.  Only applied to negbinom modalities.
5745    fdr_df : pd.DataFrame, optional
5746        A ``trans_summary`` DataFrame with ``fdr_alpha``, ``fdr_beta``, and
5747        ``is_dependent`` columns (e.g. the output of ``save_trans_summary``).
5748        Used for three purposes:
5749        (1) filtering to dependent features via the ``is_dependent`` column when
5750        ``only_dependent=True``,
5751        (2) greying out FDR-inactive parameter markers in ``mark_params`` mode,
5752        (3) classifying the Hill regime for ``_compute_hill_markers``.
5753        Feature names are matched via a ``gene_name`` or ``gene`` column.
5754    fdr_threshold : float
5755        FDR threshold for classifying components as active (default: 0.05).
5756        Components with ``fdr_alpha`` or ``fdr_beta`` >= this threshold are
5757        treated as inactive.  Only used when ``fdr_df`` is provided.
5758    **kwargs
5759        Additional plotting arguments
5760
5761    Returns
5762    -------
5763    plt.Figure or plt.Axes
5764        Matplotlib figure or axes object
5765
5766    Raises
5767    ------
5768    ValueError
5769        If x_true not set (must run fit_cis first)
5770        If feature not found in modality
5771        If show_correction='corrected' but fit_technical not run
5772
5773    Warnings
5774    --------
5775    If fit_technical not run for modality and show_correction='corrected',
5776    warns and plots uncorrected only.
5777
5778    Examples
5779    --------
5780    >>> # Plot single gene with Hill function
5781    >>> model.plot_xy_data('TET2', window=100, show_hill_function=True)
5782    >>>
5783    >>> # Plot specific splice junction with min_counts filter
5784    >>> model.plot_xy_data('chr1:12345:67890:+', modality_name='splicing_sj',
5785    ...                     min_counts=5)
5786    >>>
5787    >>> # Plot all splice junctions for a gene (creates multi-panel figure)
5788    >>> model.plot_xy_data('HES4', modality_name='splicing_sj')
5789    >>>
5790    >>> # Plot with custom colors
5791    >>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B', color_palette={'K562': 'red', 'TF1': 'blue'})
5792    >>>
5793    >>> # Show both corrected and uncorrected (default)
5794    >>> model.plot_xy_data('TET2', show_correction='both')
5795    >>>
5796    >>> # Plot with NTC gradient coloring
5797    >>> model.plot_xy_data('TET2', show_ntc_gradient=True, show_correction='uncorrected')
5798    >>>
5799    >>> # Plot only NTC cells
5800    >>> model.plot_xy_data('TET2', subset_meta={'target': 'ntc'})
5801    >>>
5802    >>> # Plot only cells from one group
5803    >>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B', subset_meta={'cell_line': 'K562'})
5804    >>>
5805    >>> # Drop a specific list of cells (e.g. flagged by check_systematic_shift)
5806    >>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B', exclude_cells=exclude_cells)
5807    >>>
5808    >>> # Plot all junctions for a gene, but only show dependent ones (n_a or n_b CI excludes 0)
5809    >>> model.plot_xy_data('HES4', modality_name='splicing_sj', only_dependent=True, ci_level=95.0)
5810    >>>
5811    >>> # ── color_by examples ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
5812    >>> # Color by NTC vs targeting instead of technical group
5813    >>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B', color_by='targeting')
5814    >>>
5815    >>> # Color by any column in model.meta (warns if continuous or >30 unique values)
5816    >>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B', color_by='cell_line')
5817    >>>
5818    >>> # Cross-product: hue = technical group, shade = NTC vs targeting
5819    >>> # NTC cells are drawn as a light tint of the group colour;
5820    >>> # targeting cells as the full colour.
5821    >>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B', color_by=['technical_group', 'targeting'])
5822    >>>
5823    >>> # Cross-product with a custom secondary grouping
5824    >>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B', color_by=['cell_line', 'perturbation_type'])
5825    >>>
5826    >>> # ── facet_by: 1-column (values → columns) ────────────────────────────
5827    >>> # One column-group of panels per cell line
5828    >>> # Grid: 1 row × (n_cell_lines × 2) cols  (default show_correction='both')
5829    >>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B', facet_by='cell_line')
5830    >>>
5831    >>> # Facet by cell line, show only corrected, log2FC mode
5832    >>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B',
5833    ...     facet_by='cell_line',
5834    ...     show_correction='corrected',
5835    ...     log2fc=True)
5836    >>>
5837    >>> # Facet by cell line AND color by NTC vs targeting within each facet panel
5838    >>> # Grid: 1 row × n_cell_lines cols; two lines per panel (NTC / Targeting)
5839    >>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B',
5840    ...     facet_by='cell_line',
5841    ...     color_by='targeting',
5842    ...     show_correction='corrected',
5843    ...     legend_outside=True)   # recommended when many panels
5844    >>>
5845    >>> # First restrict to CRISPRi guides, then facet by cell line within that subset
5846    >>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B',
5847    ...     subset_meta={'guide_type': 'CRISPRi'},
5848    ...     facet_by='cell_line')
5849    >>>
5850    >>> # ── facet_by: 2-column (proper row × col grid) ────────────────────────
5851    >>> # First column → row groups, second column → column groups
5852    >>> # Grid: n_cell_lines rows × n_perturbation_types cols (each corrected only)
5853    >>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B',
5854    ...     facet_by=['cell_line', 'perturbation_type'],
5855    ...     show_correction='corrected')
5856    >>>
5857    >>> # 2-D facet with color_by and log2FC; legend outside the grid
5858    >>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B',
5859    ...     facet_by=['cell_line', 'perturbation_type'],
5860    ...     color_by='targeting',
5861    ...     show_correction='corrected',
5862    ...     log2fc=True,
5863    ...     legend_outside=True)
5864    >>>
5865    >>> # Multi-feature + 1-D facet: rows = features, cols = facets × corrections
5866    >>> model.plot_xy_data('HES4', modality_name='splicing_sj',
5867    ...     facet_by='cell_line',
5868    ...     show_correction='corrected',
5869    ...     only_dependent=True)
5870    >>>
5871    >>> # Multi-feature + 2-D facet:
5872    >>> # rows = n_cell_lines × n_features,  cols = n_perturb_types × n_corrections
5873    >>> model.plot_xy_data('HES4', modality_name='splicing_sj',
5874    ...     facet_by=['cell_line', 'perturbation_type'],
5875    ...     show_correction='corrected',
5876    ...     only_dependent=True)
5877    """
5878    # Check x_true is set
5879    if not hasattr(model, 'x_true') or model.x_true is None:
5880        raise ValueError(
5881            "x_true not set. Must run fit_cis() before plotting x-y data.\n"
5882            "Example: model.fit_cis(sum_factor_col='sum_factor')"
5883        )
5884
5885    # Check technical_group_code is set (only required if showing correction)
5886    # Auto-fallback to uncorrected if technical groups not available
5887    has_technical_groups = 'technical_group_code' in model.meta.columns
5888
5889    if show_correction in ['corrected', 'both']:
5890        if not has_technical_groups:
5891            import warnings
5892            warnings.warn(
5893                f"technical_group_code not set, falling back to show_correction='uncorrected'. "
5894                f"To show correction, run model.set_technical_groups(['cell_line']) first.",
5895                UserWarning
5896            )
5897            show_correction = 'uncorrected'
5898
5899    # Get x_true
5900    x2d = _to_2d(model.x_true)
5901    x_true = x2d.mean(axis=0) if x2d.ndim == 2 else x2d.ravel()
5902
5903    # Reorder if needed
5904    if src_barcodes is not None:
5905        cell_barcodes = model.meta['cell'].values if 'cell' in model.meta.columns else model.meta.index.values
5906        x_true = reorder_xtrue_by_barcode(x_true, src_barcodes, cell_barcodes)
5907
5908    # Apply metadata subsetting
5909    subset_mask = None
5910    if subset_meta is not None:
5911        # Create mask based on subset_meta conditions (AND logic)
5912        subset_mask = np.ones(len(model.meta), dtype=bool)
5913        for col, value in subset_meta.items():
5914            if col not in model.meta.columns:
5915                raise ValueError(f"Column '{col}' not found in model.meta. Available columns: {list(model.meta.columns)}")
5916            subset_mask &= (model.meta[col] == value).values
5917
5918    if exclude_cells is not None:
5919        if subset_mask is None:
5920            subset_mask = np.ones(len(model.meta), dtype=bool)
5921        cell_col = model.meta['cell'].values if 'cell' in model.meta.columns else model.meta.index.values
5922        excl_mask = np.isin(cell_col, list(exclude_cells))
5923        subset_mask &= ~excl_mask
5924        print(f"[SUBSET] Excluding {excl_mask.sum()} cells via exclude_cells")
5925
5926    if subset_mask is not None:
5927        n_cells_before = len(model.meta)
5928        n_cells_after = subset_mask.sum()
5929        if n_cells_after == 0:
5930            raise ValueError(f"No cells remain after subset_meta={subset_meta} / exclude_cells filtering.")
5931
5932        if subset_meta is not None:
5933            print(f"[SUBSET] Filtering {n_cells_before} → {n_cells_after} cells based on {subset_meta}")
5934
5935        # NOTE: Don't subset x_true here - let _align_cells_to_modality() handle it
5936        # (subsetting here causes IndexError when mask is applied again in alignment)
5937
5938    # Resolve facet groups (if facet_by is set).
5939    # facet_by can be a single column name (str) or a list of 1-2 column names.
5940    #   1 column  → all unique values become column groups (existing behaviour)
5941    #   2 columns → first column → row groups, second column → column groups (2-D grid)
5942    # Each group is a (label, boolean_mask on model.meta rows) pair.
5943    facet_col_groups = None   # unique values of the *column* facet dimension
5944    facet_row_groups = None   # unique values of the *row* facet dimension (2-column only)
5945    _facet_by_list: List[str] = []  # normalised list, used for title-building later
5946
5947    if facet_by is not None:
5948        _facet_by_list = [facet_by] if isinstance(facet_by, str) else list(facet_by)
5949        if len(_facet_by_list) > 2:
5950            raise ValueError(
5951                f"facet_by supports at most 2 columns (got {len(_facet_by_list)}). "
5952                f"Pass a string for a 1-D column facet, or a list of two strings for a "
5953                f"2-D row × column facet grid."
5954            )
5955
5956        def _resolve_facet_col(col: str, role: str):
5957            """Return [(label, mask), ...] for one facet column; warn on edge cases.
5958
5959            Supports the same special keywords as color_by:
5960              'targeting'       → two groups: NTC / Targeting
5961              'technical_group' → one group per technical_group_code
5962            Any other value is looked up as a column in model.meta.
5963            """
5964            # ── Special keyword: 'targeting' ──────────────────────────────────
5965            if col == 'targeting':
5966                if 'target' not in model.meta.columns:
5967                    raise ValueError(
5968                        "facet_by='targeting' requires a 'target' column in model.meta."
5969                    )
5970                ntc_mask = (model.meta['target'].str.lower() == 'ntc').values
5971                return [('NTC', ntc_mask), ('Targeting', ~ntc_mask)]
5972
5973            # ── Special keyword: 'technical_group' ────────────────────────────
5974            if col == 'technical_group':
5975                if 'technical_group_code' not in model.meta.columns:
5976                    warnings.warn(
5977                        "facet_by='technical_group' requires technical_group_code in "
5978                        "model.meta. Using a single 'All' group.",
5979                        UserWarning
5980                    )
5981                    return [('All', np.ones(len(model.meta), dtype=bool))]
5982                grp_labels = get_technical_group_labels(model)
5983                codes = np.sort(model.meta['technical_group_code'].unique())
5984                return [
5985                    (grp_labels[int(c)] if int(c) < len(grp_labels) else str(int(c)),
5986                     (model.meta['technical_group_code'] == c).values)
5987                    for c in codes
5988                ]
5989
5990            # ── Regular model.meta column ─────────────────────────────────────
5991            if col not in model.meta.columns:
5992                raise ValueError(
5993                    f"facet_by column '{col}' not found in model.meta. "
5994                    f"Available columns: {list(model.meta.columns)}\n"
5995                    f"Special keywords also accepted: 'targeting', 'technical_group'."
5996                )
5997            fvals = sorted(model.meta[col].dropna().unique(), key=str)
5998            n_uniq = len(fvals)
5999            if n_uniq > 20:
6000                warnings.warn(
6001                    f"facet_by='{col}' ({role}) has {n_uniq} unique values — this will "
6002                    f"create {n_uniq} panel {role}s. Consider a coarser grouping.",
6003                    UserWarning
6004                )
6005            elif n_uniq <= 1:
6006                warnings.warn(
6007                    f"facet_by='{col}' has {n_uniq} unique value(s) — faceting has no effect.",
6008                    UserWarning
6009                )
6010            return [(str(v), (model.meta[col] == v).values) for v in fvals]
6011
6012        if len(_facet_by_list) == 1:
6013            facet_col_groups = _resolve_facet_col(_facet_by_list[0], 'column')
6014        else:
6015            # Two columns: first → row groups, second → column groups
6016            facet_row_groups = _resolve_facet_col(_facet_by_list[0], 'row')
6017            facet_col_groups = _resolve_facet_col(_facet_by_list[1], 'column')
6018
6019    # Get modality
6020    if modality_name is None:
6021        modality_name = model.primary_modality
6022    modality = model.get_modality(modality_name)
6023    distribution = modality.distribution
6024
6025    # Set distribution-specific default for min_counts
6026    if min_counts is None:
6027        if modality.distribution == 'negbinom':
6028            min_counts = 0  # Include all cells for gene expression
6029        else:
6030            min_counts = 3  # Require min counts for binomial/multinomial
6031
6032    # Get color palette
6033    if color_palette is None:
6034        group_labels = get_technical_group_labels(model)
6035        color_palette = get_default_color_palette(group_labels)
6036
6037    # Resolve feature(s) - could be single feature or gene name
6038    feature_indices, feature_names_resolved, is_gene = _resolve_features(feature, modality)
6039
6040    # Filter to only dependent features if requested (multifeature mode only)
6041    if only_dependent and is_gene and len(feature_indices) > 1:
6042        n_before = len(feature_indices)
6043
6044        if fdr_df is not None:
6045            # Use the precomputed is_dependent column (FDR-significant AND the
6046            # corresponding Hill exponent's CI excludes 0) rather than recomputing
6047            # a weaker FDR-only criterion here.
6048            if 'feature' not in fdr_df.columns or 'is_dependent' not in fdr_df.columns:
6049                warnings.warn(
6050                    "fdr_df must have 'feature' and 'is_dependent' columns "
6051                    "(as produced by save_trans_summary). Showing all features instead.",
6052                    UserWarning
6053                )
6054            elif not fdr_df['feature'].is_unique:
6055                _dupes = fdr_df['feature'][fdr_df['feature'].duplicated()].unique().tolist()
6056                raise ValueError(
6057                    f"fdr_df['feature'] is not unique ({len(_dupes)} duplicated value(s), "
6058                    f"e.g. {_dupes[:5]}) — a per-feature lookup would silently use only "
6059                    "the last matching row. This likely means fdr_df was saved by an "
6060                    "older/buggy version of save_trans_summary; regenerate it."
6061                )
6062            else:
6063                dep_lookup = dict(zip(fdr_df['feature'], fdr_df['is_dependent']))
6064
6065                kept_indices = []
6066                kept_names = []
6067                for idx, name in zip(feature_indices, feature_names_resolved):
6068                    dep_val = dep_lookup.get(name, np.nan)
6069                    if pd.notna(dep_val) and bool(dep_val):
6070                        kept_indices.append(idx)
6071                        kept_names.append(name)
6072
6073                if len(kept_indices) == 0:
6074                    warnings.warn(
6075                        f"No features have is_dependent=True for '{feature}'. "
6076                        f"Showing all {n_before} features instead.",
6077                        UserWarning
6078                    )
6079                else:
6080                    feature_indices = kept_indices
6081                    feature_names_resolved = kept_names
6082                    print(f"[DEPENDENCY FILTER] {feature}: {n_before} → {len(feature_indices)} features "
6083                          f"(is_dependent=True)")
6084
6085        else:
6086            # Fallback: CI-based filtering on n_a / n_b from posterior samples.
6087            # Requires fit_trans() with function_type='additive_hill'.
6088            if modality_name == model.primary_modality:
6089                posterior = getattr(model, 'posterior_samples_trans', None)
6090            else:
6091                posterior = getattr(modality, 'posterior_samples_trans', None)
6092
6093            if posterior is None:
6094                warnings.warn(
6095                    "only_dependent=True requires fit_trans() to have been run "
6096                    f"(modality='{modality_name}'). Showing all features instead.",
6097                    UserWarning
6098                )
6099            elif 'n_a' not in posterior or 'n_b' not in posterior:
6100                warnings.warn(
6101                    "only_dependent=True without fdr_df requires fit_trans() with "
6102                    "function_type='additive_hill' (needs n_a/n_b). "
6103                    "Showing all features instead.",
6104                    UserWarning
6105                )
6106            else:
6107                n_a_samps = posterior['n_a'].detach().cpu().numpy()
6108                n_b_samps = posterior['n_b'].detach().cpu().numpy()
6109                if n_a_samps.ndim == 3:
6110                    n_a_samps = n_a_samps.squeeze(1)
6111                    n_b_samps = n_b_samps.squeeze(1)
6112
6113                dep_mask_a = dependency_mask_from_n(n_a_samps, ci=ci_level)
6114                dep_mask_b = dependency_mask_from_n(n_b_samps, ci=ci_level)
6115                dep_mask = dep_mask_a | dep_mask_b
6116
6117                filtered_indices = [idx for idx in feature_indices if dep_mask[idx]]
6118                filtered_names = [name for idx, name in zip(feature_indices, feature_names_resolved)
6119                                  if dep_mask[idx]]
6120
6121                if len(filtered_indices) == 0:
6122                    warnings.warn(
6123                        f"No dependent features found for '{feature}' (all n CIs include 0). "
6124                        f"Showing all {n_before} features instead.",
6125                        UserWarning
6126                    )
6127                else:
6128                    feature_indices = filtered_indices
6129                    feature_names_resolved = filtered_names
6130                    print(f"[DEPENDENCY FILTER] {feature}: {n_before} → {len(feature_indices)} features "
6131                          f"(CI={ci_level}%, {dep_mask_a.sum()} positive, {dep_mask_b.sum()} negative)")
6132
6133    # ── Grid path: multi-feature (gene input) OR single feature with facet_by ──
6134    # Multinomial is handled separately (has its own K-category subplot layout).
6135    use_grid = (is_gene and len(feature_indices) > 1) or (facet_by is not None)
6136
6137    if use_grid:
6138        # Special handling for multinomial - needs K subplots per feature
6139        if distribution == 'multinomial':
6140            if facet_by is not None:
6141                warnings.warn(
6142                    "facet_by is not yet supported for multinomial distribution. "
6143                    "Ignoring facet_by and plotting without faceting.",
6144                    UserWarning
6145                )
6146            return _plot_multinomial_multifeature(
6147                model=model,
6148                feature_indices=feature_indices,
6149                feature_names=feature_names_resolved,
6150                gene_name=feature,
6151                modality=modality,
6152                x_true=x_true,  # full model x_true; alignment to modality cells done inside
6153                window=window,
6154                min_counts=min_counts,
6155                show_correction=show_correction,
6156                color_palette=color_palette,
6157                xlabel=xlabel,
6158                ylabel=ylabel,
6159                figsize=figsize,
6160                subset_mask=subset_mask,
6161                **kwargs
6162            )
6163
6164        # Standard grid for 2D distributions.
6165        # Layout:
6166        #   rows = n_facet_rows × n_features   (facet-row groups nest features)
6167        #   cols = n_facet_cols × n_corrections (facet-col groups nest correction mode)
6168        # When facet_by is a single column, facet_row_groups is None (n_facet_rows=1),
6169        # so the layout reduces to rows=features, cols=n_facets×n_corrections as before.
6170        n_features = len(feature_indices)
6171        corrections_list = ['uncorrected', 'corrected'] if show_correction == 'both' else [show_correction]
6172        n_corrections = len(corrections_list)
6173        n_facet_rows = len(facet_row_groups) if facet_row_groups else 1
6174        n_facet_cols = len(facet_col_groups) if facet_col_groups else 1
6175        n_rows = n_facet_rows * n_features
6176        n_cols = n_facet_cols * n_corrections
6177
6178        if figsize is None:
6179            figsize = (6 * n_cols, 3 * n_rows)
6180
6181        fig, axes = plt.subplots(n_rows, n_cols, figsize=figsize, squeeze=False,
6182                                 constrained_layout=True)
6183
6184        def _plot_one_grid(feat_name, ax, correction, mask,
6185                           ntc_x_offset=None, ntc_y_offset=None):
6186            """Plot one panel: one feature × one correction × one (optional) facet."""
6187            if distribution == 'negbinom':
6188                plot_negbinom_xy(
6189                    model=model, feature=feat_name, modality=modality,
6190                    x_true=x_true, window=window, show_correction=correction,
6191                    color_palette=color_palette, show_hill_function=show_hill_function,
6192                    show_ntc_gradient=show_ntc_gradient, sum_factor_col=sum_factor_col,
6193                    min_counts=min_counts, xlabel=xlabel, ax=ax,
6194                    subset_mask=mask, mark_params=mark_params, ci_level=ci_level,
6195                    log2fc=log2fc, reference_df=reference_df,
6196                    fdr_df=fdr_df, fdr_threshold=fdr_threshold,
6197                    color_by=color_by,
6198                    ntc_x_offset=ntc_x_offset, ntc_y_offset=ntc_y_offset,
6199                    expand_x_to_params=expand_x_to_params,
6200                    expand_y_to_params=expand_y_to_params,
6201                    ylabel=ylabel,
6202                    **kwargs
6203                )
6204            elif distribution == 'binomial':
6205                plot_binomial_xy(
6206                    model=model, feature=feat_name, modality=modality,
6207                    x_true=x_true, window=window, show_correction=correction,
6208                    min_counts=min_counts, color_palette=color_palette,
6209                    show_trans_function=show_hill_function,
6210                    show_ntc_gradient=show_ntc_gradient, xlabel=xlabel, ax=ax,
6211                    subset_mask=mask, mark_params=mark_params, ci_level=ci_level,
6212                    log2fc=log2fc, ntc_x_offset=ntc_x_offset,
6213                    ylabel=ylabel,
6214                    **kwargs
6215                )
6216            elif distribution in ('normal', 'studentt'):
6217                plot_normal_xy(
6218                    model=model, feature=feat_name, modality=modality,
6219                    x_true=x_true, window=window, show_correction=correction,
6220                    color_palette=color_palette, show_trans_function=show_hill_function,
6221                    show_ntc_gradient=show_ntc_gradient, xlabel=xlabel, ax=ax,
6222                    subset_mask=mask, mark_params=mark_params, ci_level=ci_level,
6223                    log2fc=log2fc, ntc_x_offset=ntc_x_offset,
6224                    ylabel=ylabel,
6225                    **kwargs
6226                )
6227            else:
6228                ax.text(0.5, 0.5, f"Grid not supported for {distribution}",
6229                        ha='center', va='center', transform=ax.transAxes)
6230
6231        # Iterate: features (outer) → row-facets → col-facets → corrections.
6232        # Features are outer so we can compute the global NTC log2FC offsets once per
6233        # feature (using the global subset_mask, not any facet mask) and reuse them
6234        # across all facet panels — ensuring the NTC reference is consistent even when
6235        # a facet panel contains no NTC cells (e.g. a "Targeting" column facet).
6236        facet_col_iter = facet_col_groups if facet_col_groups else [(None, None)]
6237        facet_row_iter = facet_row_groups if facet_row_groups else [(None, None)]
6238
6239        _axes_by_feat = {feat_i: [] for feat_i in range(n_features)}
6240
6241        for feat_i, feat_name in enumerate(feature_names_resolved):
6242            # Pre-compute global NTC log2FC offsets for this feature. x_offset is
6243            # distribution-agnostic (log2 of mean NTC x_true); y_offset is only
6244            # meaningful/used for negbinom (other distributions keep their y-axis
6245            # as-is -- only the x-axis becomes log2FC when log2fc=True).
6246            if log2fc:
6247                _ntc_x_off, _ntc_y_off = _compute_global_log2fc_offsets(
6248                    model, modality, feat_name, x_true, subset_mask, sum_factor_col
6249                )
6250            else:
6251                _ntc_x_off = _ntc_y_off = None
6252
6253            for frow_i, (frow_label, frow_mask) in enumerate(facet_row_iter):
6254                grid_row = frow_i * n_features + feat_i
6255                for fcol_i, (fcol_label, fcol_mask) in enumerate(facet_col_iter):
6256                    # Combine all masks (global subset_mask AND row-facet AND col-facet)
6257                    combined_mask = subset_mask
6258                    for m in [frow_mask, fcol_mask]:
6259                        if m is not None:
6260                            combined_mask = (combined_mask & m
6261                                             if combined_mask is not None else m)
6262
6263                    for corr_i, correction in enumerate(corrections_list):
6264                        grid_col = fcol_i * n_corrections + corr_i
6265                        ax = axes[grid_row, grid_col]
6266                        _plot_one_grid(feat_name, ax, correction, combined_mask,
6267                                       ntc_x_offset=_ntc_x_off, ntc_y_offset=_ntc_y_off)
6268                        _axes_by_feat[feat_i].append(ax)
6269                        # Strip the per-panel legend — one shared legend is drawn below
6270                        if ax.get_legend() is not None:
6271                            ax.get_legend().remove()
6272                        # Build title prefix from active facet labels
6273                        title_parts = []
6274                        if frow_label is not None:
6275                            title_parts.append(f"{_facet_by_list[0]}={frow_label}")
6276                        if fcol_label is not None:
6277                            col_key = (_facet_by_list[1] if len(_facet_by_list) > 1
6278                                       else _facet_by_list[0])
6279                            title_parts.append(f"{col_key}={fcol_label}")
6280                        if title_parts:
6281                            current_title = ax.get_title()
6282                            ax.set_title("  ".join(title_parts) + "\n" + current_title)
6283
6284        # ── Uniform axis limits across panels ────────────────────────────────
6285        # Each panel has already set its own limits via set_xlim / set_ylim.
6286        # The x-axis (cis gene expression) is shared across all panels so
6287        # dose-response curves line up. The y-axis is only shared *within*
6288        # a feature (across its facet-row/col/correction panels), not across
6289        # different features — different features (e.g. different SJs) can
6290        # have very different effect magnitudes, and forcing a common y-axis
6291        # hides subtle effects in the smaller-magnitude ones.
6292        _all_xlims = []
6293        for _ax in axes.ravel():
6294            # Skip axes that have no plotted lines (empty panels)
6295            if not _ax.lines and not _ax.collections:
6296                continue
6297            _all_xlims.append(_ax.get_xlim())
6298        if _all_xlims:
6299            _shared_x = (min(lo for lo, hi in _all_xlims),
6300                         max(hi for lo, hi in _all_xlims))
6301            for _ax in axes.ravel():
6302                _ax.set_xlim(_shared_x)
6303
6304        for _feat_axes in _axes_by_feat.values():
6305            _feat_ylims = [_ax.get_ylim() for _ax in _feat_axes
6306                           if _ax.lines or _ax.collections]
6307            if not _feat_ylims:
6308                continue
6309            _feat_shared_y = (min(lo for lo, hi in _feat_ylims),
6310                               max(hi for lo, hi in _feat_ylims))
6311            for _ax in _feat_axes:
6312                _ax.set_ylim(_feat_shared_y)
6313
6314        # Overall suptitle for multi-feature plots
6315        if is_gene and len(feature_indices) > 1:
6316            plt.suptitle(
6317                f"{model.cis_gene} → {feature} (gene, n={len(feature_indices)} features)"
6318            )
6319
6320        # One shared legend for the whole grid (no duplicates across panels).
6321        handles, labels = _collect_legend_handles(axes.ravel())
6322        if handles:
6323            if legend_outside:
6324                # Anchor to the right edge of the figure (transFigure coords)
6325                fig.legend(handles, labels, bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 0.5),
6326                           loc='center left', frameon=False)
6327            else:
6328                axes[-1, -1].legend(handles, labels, frameon=False)
6329
6330        _save_figure(fig, model, filename)
6331        return fig
6332
6333    # ── Single-feature path (no faceting) ─────────────────────────────────────
6334    feature = feature_names_resolved[0]  # Use resolved feature name
6335
6336    # Pre-compute global NTC log2FC offsets (same approach as grid path). x_offset
6337    # is distribution-agnostic (log2 of mean NTC x_true) and used by every
6338    # distribution when log2fc=True; y_offset is only meaningful for negbinom
6339    # (other distributions leave their y-axis as-is -- only x becomes log2FC).
6340    # This ensures the NTC reference is computed from ALL NTC cells (ignoring
6341    # min_counts and color_by grouping), making it independent of which colour
6342    # or subset is shown.
6343    _sf_ntc_x_off = _sf_ntc_y_off = None
6344    if log2fc:
6345        _sf_ntc_x_off, _sf_ntc_y_off = _compute_global_log2fc_offsets(
6346            model, modality, feature, x_true, subset_mask, sum_factor_col
6347        )
6348
6349    if distribution == 'negbinom':
6350        result = plot_negbinom_xy(
6351            model=model,
6352            feature=feature,
6353            modality=modality,
6354            x_true=x_true,
6355            window=window,
6356            show_correction=show_correction,
6357            color_palette=color_palette,
6358            show_hill_function=show_hill_function,
6359            show_ntc_gradient=show_ntc_gradient,
6360            sum_factor_col=sum_factor_col,
6361            min_counts=min_counts,
6362            xlabel=xlabel,
6363            subset_mask=subset_mask,
6364            mark_params=mark_params,
6365            ci_level=ci_level,
6366            legend_outside=legend_outside,
6367            figsize=figsize,
6368            log2fc=log2fc,
6369            reference_df=reference_df,
6370            fdr_df=fdr_df,
6371            fdr_threshold=fdr_threshold,
6372            color_by=color_by,
6373            ntc_x_offset=_sf_ntc_x_off,
6374            ntc_y_offset=_sf_ntc_y_off,
6375            expand_x_to_params=expand_x_to_params,
6376            expand_y_to_params=expand_y_to_params,
6377            ylabel=ylabel,
6378            **kwargs
6379        )
6380
6381    elif distribution == 'binomial':
6382        result = plot_binomial_xy(
6383            model=model,
6384            feature=feature,
6385            modality=modality,
6386            x_true=x_true,
6387            window=window,
6388            show_correction=show_correction,
6389            min_counts=min_counts,
6390            color_palette=color_palette,
6391            show_trans_function=show_hill_function,
6392            show_ntc_gradient=show_ntc_gradient,
6393            xlabel=xlabel,
6394            subset_mask=subset_mask,
6395            mark_params=mark_params,
6396            ci_level=ci_level,
6397            legend_outside=legend_outside,
6398            figsize=figsize,
6399            log2fc=log2fc,
6400            ntc_x_offset=_sf_ntc_x_off,
6401            ylabel=ylabel,
6402            **kwargs
6403        )
6404
6405    elif distribution == 'multinomial':
6406        result = plot_multinomial_xy(
6407            model=model,
6408            feature=feature,
6409            modality=modality,
6410            x_true=x_true,
6411            window=window,
6412            min_counts=min_counts,
6413            show_correction=show_correction,
6414            color_palette=color_palette,
6415            show_trans_function=show_hill_function,
6416            show_ntc_gradient=show_ntc_gradient,
6417            xlabel=xlabel,
6418            figsize=figsize,
6419            subset_mask=subset_mask,
6420            log2fc=log2fc,
6421            ntc_x_offset=_sf_ntc_x_off,
6422            ylabel=ylabel,
6423            **kwargs
6424        )
6425
6426    elif distribution in ('normal', 'studentt'):
6427        result = plot_normal_xy(
6428            model=model,
6429            feature=feature,
6430            modality=modality,
6431            x_true=x_true,
6432            window=window,
6433            show_correction=show_correction,
6434            color_palette=color_palette,
6435            show_trans_function=show_hill_function,
6436            show_ntc_gradient=show_ntc_gradient,
6437            xlabel=xlabel,
6438            subset_mask=subset_mask,
6439            mark_params=mark_params,
6440            ci_level=ci_level,
6441            legend_outside=legend_outside,
6442            figsize=figsize,
6443            log2fc=log2fc,
6444            ntc_x_offset=_sf_ntc_x_off,
6445            ylabel=ylabel,
6446            **kwargs
6447        )
6448
6449    else:
6450        raise ValueError(f"Plotting not implemented for distribution '{distribution}'")
6451
6452    # Save single-feature figure
6453    if filename is not None:
6454        ax_result = result if isinstance(result, plt.Axes) else result[0]
6455        _save_figure(ax_result.get_figure(), model, filename)
6456    return result

Plot raw x-y data showing relationship between cis gene expression and modality values.

Requires x_true to be set (must run fit_cis() first).

Parameters
  • model (bayesDREAM): Fitted bayesDREAM model with x_true set
  • feature (str): Feature name (junction, donor, etc.) OR gene name.
    • If a specific feature name (e.g., 'chr1:999788:999865'), plots that feature
    • If a gene name (e.g., 'HES4'), plots all features for that gene in subplots
    • Requires modality to have gene information ('gene', 'gene_name', or 'gene_id' columns)
  • modality_name (str, optional): Modality name (default: primary modality)
  • window (int): k-NN window size for smoothing (default: 100 cells)
  • show_correction (str): 'uncorrected': no technical correction 'corrected': apply alpha_y technical correction 'both': show both side-by-side (default)
  • min_counts (int, optional): Minimum raw counts to include cells. Default depends on distribution: 0 for negbinom, 3 for binomial/multinomial. For negbinom: excludes cells with y_obs < min_counts For binomial: minimum denominator For multinomial: minimum total counts
  • color_palette (dict, optional): Custom colors for technical groups, keyed by the group label string Example: {'K562': 'crimson', 'TF1': 'dodgerblue'}
  • show_hill_function (bool): Overlay fitted trans function if trans model fitted (all distributions, default: True) Works with all function types: additive_hill, single_hill, polynomial Automatically detects function type from posterior_samples_trans
  • show_ntc_gradient (bool): Color lines by NTC proportion in k-NN window (default: False) Lighter colors = more NTC cells, Darker colors = fewer NTC cells Only applies to uncorrected plots Fully implemented for: negbinom, binomial, normal, studentt Not yet implemented for: multinomial (will issue warning)
  • sum_factor_col (str): Column name in model.meta for sum factors (default: 'sum_factor') Can be 'sum_factor', 'sum_factor_adj', or any other sum factor column Only used for negbinom distribution (gene expression)
  • xlabel (str): X-axis label (default: "log2(x_true)")
  • ylabel (str, optional): Override the y-axis label (default: None, uses a distribution-specific default -- "log2(counts)" for negbinom, "Percentage (%)" for binomial (0-100 scale), "Proportion" for multinomial (0-1 scale), "Value" for normal/studentt). The binomial default is deliberately generic since that distribution covers any bounded count/denominator ratio, not just splicing PSI -- pass e.g. ylabel='PSI (%)' for splicing modalities or ylabel='Spliced (%)' for a gene velocity modality.
  • figsize (tuple, optional): Figure size (auto-sized if None)
  • src_barcodes (np.ndarray, optional): Source barcode order if x_true not in model.meta order
  • subset_meta (dict, optional): Subset cells by metadata columns. Dictionary of {column: value} pairs. Example: {'target': 'ntc'} - plot only NTC cells Example: {'cell_line': 'K562'} - plot only K562 cells Example: {'lane': 'L1', 'cell_line': 'K562'} - plot L1 lane K562 cells Multiple conditions are combined with AND logic.
  • exclude_cells (list of str, optional): Cell names (matched against model.meta['cell']) to drop before plotting, e.g. cells identified by check_systematic_shift's exclude_cells filtering logic. AND-combined with subset_meta when both are given, without needing to call model.subset_cells() first. Example: exclude_cells=['cell_1', 'cell_2']
  • only_dependent (bool): If True and plotting multiple features (gene name), filter to only "dependent" features (default: False). When fdr_df is provided, uses its precomputed is_dependent column (FDR-significant AND the Hill coefficient's credible interval excludes 0). Otherwise falls back to filtering on the n_a/n_b credible interval alone, which requires fit_trans() to have been run with function_type='additive_hill'. Ignored for single-feature plots.
  • ci_level (float): Credible interval level for dependency filtering and parameter marker classification (default: 95.0). Used by only_dependent=True and mark_params=True.
  • mark_params (bool or str): Overlay meaningful parameter markers on the Hill function (default: False). Requires show_hill_function=True and fit_trans() completed with function_type='single_hill' or 'additive_hill'.
    • True or 'both': markers for both the fitted curve and the reference curve
    • 'fit': markers for the fitted curve only
    • 'reference': markers for the reference curve only (requires reference_df)
    • False or None: no markers Markers drawn depend on the fitted regime:
    • Single Hill / effectively single: log2(A), log2(A+α·Vmax), log2(EC50)
    • Same-sign additive (both Hills in same direction): log2(A), log2(A+α·Vmax_a+β·Vmax_b), log2(EC50_lower), log2(EC50_upper)
    • Non-monotonic (opposite-sign Hills): log2(y: x→0), log2(y: x→∞), log2(EC50_lower), log2(EC50_upper); additionally log2(A+α·Vmax_a+β·Vmax_b) [peak] if activation EC50 < inhibition EC50 For non-negbinom distributions, all y-axis markers are in linear space. Note: asymptotes include the α/β weight factors (e.g. A+α·Vmax, not A+Vmax).
  • log2fc (bool): If True, x-axis becomes log2(x_true) - log2(mean NTC x_true) (log2FC relative to NTC) instead of raw log2(x_true) (default: False). For negbinom, the y-axis also becomes log2FC relative to NTC (log2(counts) - log2(mean NTC counts, reference group)), and a grey dotted crosshair is drawn at (0, 0). For binomial/normal/studentt/multinomial, only the x-axis transforms -- the y-axis is left in its natural scale (PSI%, raw value, proportion), since there's no natural log2FC transform for a bounded/non-count quantity. Only a vertical grey dotted line is drawn at x=0 to mark the NTC reference.
  • color_by (str or list of two str): What to color smoothed lines by (default: 'technical_group').
    • 'technical_group': one line per cell-line / technical group (default)
    • 'targeting': two lines — NTC vs Targeting
    • Any column name in model.meta: one line per unique value. A warning is issued if the column looks continuous (float dtype with many unique values) or has more than 30 unique values.
    • List of two (e.g. ['technical_group', 'targeting']): cross-product of two groupings — the first sets hue, the second sets shade. When the secondary is 'targeting', NTC lines are drawn as a light tint of the group colour and targeting lines as the full colour (matching the classic "shades" style). Override any auto-generated colour via color_palette using the combined label "K562 / NTC", "K562 / Targeting", etc. Alpha-y technical correction is always applied per technical group regardless of this setting.

  • facet_by (str or list of str, optional): Column name(s) to facet by (default: None). Accepts either a single string or a list of at most two strings. Each value may be a real column name in model.meta or one of the same special keywords supported by color_by:

    • 'targeting' — two panels: NTC / Targeting (derived from model.meta['target'])
    • 'technical_group' — one panel per technical group code

    Analogous to facet_grid in ggplot2.

    1 column (facet_by='cell_line') — all unique values become side-by-side column groups::

    rows = n_features,  cols = n_facets × n_corrections

    Example: 3 cell lines + show_correction='both' → 1 × 6 grid [K562 uncorr | K562 corr | TF1 uncorr | TF1 corr | HL60 uncorr | HL60 corr]

    2 columns (facet_by=['cell_line', 'perturbation']) — first column maps to grid rows, second column maps to grid columns::

    rows = n_facet1_values × n_features
cols = n_facet2_values × n_corrections

    Example: 3 cell lines × 2 perturbation types + show_correction='corrected' → 3 × 2 grid (cell lines as rows, perturbation types as columns).

    Combining with other parameters:

    • subset_meta / exclude_cells: each facet mask is AND-combined with the global subset_meta / exclude_cells filters, so you can first narrow to CRISPRi cells (or drop specific cells) and then facet by cell line within that subset.
    • color_by: works independently within each panel — e.g. facet_by='cell_line' splits cell lines into columns while color_by='targeting' still draws NTC / Targeting lines inside each panel.
    • legend_outside=True: recommended when faceting produces many panels, to keep the shared legend out of the plot area.

    Facet labels appear as the first line of each panel title, e.g. cell_line=K562 or cell_line=K562 perturbation=CRISPRi. A warning is issued for columns with more than 20 unique values. Not yet supported for multinomial distributions (ignored with a warning in that case).

  • expand_x_to_params (bool): When True, extend the x-axis (and the Hill curve) beyond the data range so that all K/EC50 parameters are visible on the plot (default: False). Requires show_hill_function=True and a fitted trans model. The x-axis minimum and maximum are widened to include the mean K_a and K_b values from the posterior, so any EC50 that falls outside the data range will still appear on the curve. Ignored for polynomial function types (which have no K parameters).
  • expand_y_to_params (bool): When True, extend the y-axis to show the full range of the fitted Hill curve over the entire displayed x range, including any x values added by expand_x_to_params (default: False). Normally the Hill curve's y values are only used for y-axis scaling within the data x range; this flag removes that restriction so the y-axis accommodates the Hill curve's y values at K/EC50 positions and at the asymptotes.
  • legend_outside (bool): Place the legend outside the panel to the right, shared across all panels (default: False). Useful when many lines clutter the plot area.
  • filename (str, optional): If provided, save the figure to model.output_dir / filename. A .png extension is added automatically if none is given. Use a full path to save elsewhere.
  • figsize (tuple, optional): Figure size as (width, height) in inches. When None (default) the size is chosen automatically: 6 inches per column × 3 inches per row for multi-panel plots, or (8, 5) / (14, 5) for single-panel plots.
  • reference_df (pd.DataFrame, optional): A trans_summary DataFrame whose rows contain fitted Hill parameters (columns ending in _median, e.g. A_median, Vmax_a_median, etc.). When provided, a reference Hill curve is overlaid in red dashed on each negbinom panel. The feature name is matched via a gene_name or gene column. Only applied to negbinom modalities.
  • fdr_df (pd.DataFrame, optional): A trans_summary DataFrame with fdr_alpha, fdr_beta, and is_dependent columns (e.g. the output of save_trans_summary). Used for three purposes: (1) filtering to dependent features via the is_dependent column when only_dependent=True, (2) greying out FDR-inactive parameter markers in mark_params mode, (3) classifying the Hill regime for _compute_hill_markers. Feature names are matched via a gene_name or gene column.
  • fdr_threshold (float): FDR threshold for classifying components as active (default: 0.05). Components with fdr_alpha or fdr_beta >= this threshold are treated as inactive. Only used when fdr_df is provided.
  • **kwargs: Additional plotting arguments
Returns
  • plt.Figure or plt.Axes: Matplotlib figure or axes object
Raises
  • ValueError: If x_true not set (must run fit_cis first) If feature not found in modality If show_correction='corrected' but fit_technical not run
Warnings

If fit_technical not run for modality and show_correction='corrected', warns and plots uncorrected only.

Examples
>>> # Plot single gene with Hill function
>>> model.plot_xy_data('TET2', window=100, show_hill_function=True)
>>>
>>> # Plot specific splice junction with min_counts filter
>>> model.plot_xy_data('chr1:12345:67890:+', modality_name='splicing_sj',
...                     min_counts=5)
>>>
>>> # Plot all splice junctions for a gene (creates multi-panel figure)
>>> model.plot_xy_data('HES4', modality_name='splicing_sj')
>>>
>>> # Plot with custom colors
>>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B', color_palette={'K562': 'red', 'TF1': 'blue'})
>>>
>>> # Show both corrected and uncorrected (default)
>>> model.plot_xy_data('TET2', show_correction='both')
>>>
>>> # Plot with NTC gradient coloring
>>> model.plot_xy_data('TET2', show_ntc_gradient=True, show_correction='uncorrected')
>>>
>>> # Plot only NTC cells
>>> model.plot_xy_data('TET2', subset_meta={'target': 'ntc'})
>>>
>>> # Plot only cells from one group
>>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B', subset_meta={'cell_line': 'K562'})
>>>
>>> # Drop a specific list of cells (e.g. flagged by check_systematic_shift)
>>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B', exclude_cells=exclude_cells)
>>>
>>> # Plot all junctions for a gene, but only show dependent ones (n_a or n_b CI excludes 0)
>>> model.plot_xy_data('HES4', modality_name='splicing_sj', only_dependent=True, ci_level=95.0)
>>>
>>> # ── color_by examples ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
>>> # Color by NTC vs targeting instead of technical group
>>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B', color_by='targeting')
>>>
>>> # Color by any column in model.meta (warns if continuous or >30 unique values)
>>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B', color_by='cell_line')
>>>
>>> # Cross-product: hue = technical group, shade = NTC vs targeting
>>> # NTC cells are drawn as a light tint of the group colour;
>>> # targeting cells as the full colour.
>>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B', color_by=['technical_group', 'targeting'])
>>>
>>> # Cross-product with a custom secondary grouping
>>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B', color_by=['cell_line', 'perturbation_type'])
>>>
>>> # ── facet_by: 1-column (values → columns) ────────────────────────────
>>> # One column-group of panels per cell line
>>> # Grid: 1 row × (n_cell_lines × 2) cols  (default show_correction='both')
>>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B', facet_by='cell_line')
>>>
>>> # Facet by cell line, show only corrected, log2FC mode
>>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B',
...     facet_by='cell_line',
...     show_correction='corrected',
...     log2fc=True)
>>>
>>> # Facet by cell line AND color by NTC vs targeting within each facet panel
>>> # Grid: 1 row × n_cell_lines cols; two lines per panel (NTC / Targeting)
>>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B',
...     facet_by='cell_line',
...     color_by='targeting',
...     show_correction='corrected',
...     legend_outside=True)   # recommended when many panels
>>>
>>> # First restrict to CRISPRi guides, then facet by cell line within that subset
>>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B',
...     subset_meta={'guide_type': 'CRISPRi'},
...     facet_by='cell_line')
>>>
>>> # ── facet_by: 2-column (proper row × col grid) ────────────────────────
>>> # First column → row groups, second column → column groups
>>> # Grid: n_cell_lines rows × n_perturbation_types cols (each corrected only)
>>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B',
...     facet_by=['cell_line', 'perturbation_type'],
...     show_correction='corrected')
>>>
>>> # 2-D facet with color_by and log2FC; legend outside the grid
>>> model.plot_xy_data('GFI1B',
...     facet_by=['cell_line', 'perturbation_type'],
...     color_by='targeting',
...     show_correction='corrected',
...     log2fc=True,
...     legend_outside=True)
>>>
>>> # Multi-feature + 1-D facet: rows = features, cols = facets × corrections
>>> model.plot_xy_data('HES4', modality_name='splicing_sj',
...     facet_by='cell_line',
...     show_correction='corrected',
...     only_dependent=True)
>>>
>>> # Multi-feature + 2-D facet:
>>> # rows = n_cell_lines × n_features,  cols = n_perturb_types × n_corrections
>>> model.plot_xy_data('HES4', modality_name='splicing_sj',
...     facet_by=['cell_line', 'perturbation_type'],
...     show_correction='corrected',
...     only_dependent=True)
def restyle_targeting_lines( result, color_palette=None, ntc_alpha=0.35, ntc_linestyle='dashed', targeting_alpha=1.0, targeting_linestyle='solid', ntc_label_fragment='NTC', targeting_label_fragment='Targeting', rebuild_legend=True, legend_outside=False, legend_kwargs=None): 
6459def restyle_targeting_lines(
6460    result,
6461    color_palette=None,
6462    ntc_alpha=0.35,
6463    ntc_linestyle="dashed",
6464    targeting_alpha=1.0,
6465    targeting_linestyle="solid",
6466    ntc_label_fragment="NTC",
6467    targeting_label_fragment="Targeting",
6468    rebuild_legend=True,
6469    legend_outside=False,
6470    legend_kwargs=None,
6471):
6472    """
6473    Restyle a ``plot_xy_data()`` result to use alpha + linestyle for NTC vs
6474    targeting, ggplot ``scale_alpha_manual``/``scale_linetype_manual`` style,
6475    instead of plot_xy_data's built-in color-tint shading.
6476
6477    Meant for plotting everything on one shared axes with a single flat hue
6478    per primary group (e.g. cell_line) rather than faceting: call
6479    ``plot_xy_data`` with ``facet_by=None`` and
6480    ``color_by=['<primary>', 'targeting']`` (which labels lines
6481    ``"<primary> / NTC"`` / ``"<primary> / Targeting"`` and tints NTC as a
6482    lighter shade of the primary color), then pass the result here to flatten
6483    each line back to its primary group's solid color and encode NTC vs
6484    targeting as alpha/linestyle instead::
6485
6486        palette = {'CRISPRi': 'steelblue', 'CRISPRa': 'tomato'}
6487        result = model.plot_xy_data(
6488            'GFI1B',
6489            facet_by=None,
6490            color_by=['cell_line', 'targeting'],
6491            color_palette=palette,
6492            legend_outside=True,
6493        )
6494        restyle_targeting_lines(result, color_palette=palette, legend_outside=True)
6495
6496    Also works with plain ``color_by='targeting'`` (labels are bare
6497    ``"NTC"``/``"Targeting"``, no primary-color reset needed --
6498    ``color_palette=None`` in that case).
6499
6500    Parameters
6501    ----------
6502    result : matplotlib Figure, Axes, or array of Axes
6503        Return value of ``model.plot_xy_data(...)``.
6504    color_palette : dict, optional
6505        ``{primary_label: color}`` -- the same dict passed to
6506        ``plot_xy_data(color_palette=...)``. Used to reset each line to its
6507        primary group's flat color, undoing plot_xy_data's NTC tint. If
6508        None, colors are left as plot_xy_data drew them (tinted).
6509    ntc_alpha, targeting_alpha : float
6510        Alpha for lines whose label contains ``ntc_label_fragment`` /
6511        ``targeting_label_fragment`` respectively.
6512    ntc_linestyle, targeting_linestyle : str
6513        Matplotlib linestyle for the same two groups (e.g. ``'dashed'``,
6514        ``'solid'``).
6515    ntc_label_fragment, targeting_label_fragment : str
6516        Substrings identifying NTC vs targeting lines in their legend label.
6517        Lines whose label matches neither are left untouched.
6518    rebuild_legend : bool, default True
6519        Regenerate each axes' legend from the restyled lines. Matplotlib
6520        legends snapshot line style at creation time, so the original
6521        legend won't reflect the restyle otherwise.
6522    legend_outside : bool, default False
6523        Match whatever you passed to ``plot_xy_data(legend_outside=...)``,
6524        so the rebuilt legend is placed the same way.
6525    legend_kwargs : dict, optional
6526        Extra kwargs forwarded to the rebuilt ``legend()`` call, overriding
6527        the defaults (``frameon=False``, plus ``bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.5),
6528        loc='center left'`` when ``legend_outside=True``).
6529
6530    Returns
6531    -------
6532    The same ``result`` object, restyled in place.
6533
6534    Notes
6535    -----
6536    Only ``Line2D`` artists (the smoothed trend lines) are restyled --
6537    linestyle has no meaning for scatter points, and plot_xy_data's raw
6538    per-cell scatter points are unlabeled and left untouched.
6539
6540    This function does not raise: if ``result`` isn't a ``plt.Axes``,
6541    ``plt.Figure``, or an array/list containing ``plt.Axes`` instances, it
6542    resolves to zero axes and silently does nothing. Likewise, any axes
6543    found with no lines matching ``ntc_label_fragment``/
6544    ``targeting_label_fragment`` are left untouched.
6545    """
6546    if isinstance(result, plt.Axes):
6547        axes = [result]
6548    elif isinstance(result, plt.Figure):
6549        axes = result.axes
6550    else:
6551        axes = [a for a in np.ravel(result) if isinstance(a, plt.Axes)]
6552
6553    legend_kwargs = dict(legend_kwargs or {})
6554
6555    for ax in axes:
6556        handles, labels = [], []
6557        for line in ax.get_lines():
6558            label = line.get_label()
6559            if not label or label.startswith("_"):
6560                continue
6561
6562            if ntc_label_fragment in label:
6563                alpha, linestyle = ntc_alpha, ntc_linestyle
6564            elif targeting_label_fragment in label:
6565                alpha, linestyle = targeting_alpha, targeting_linestyle
6566            else:
6567                handles.append(line)
6568                labels.append(label)
6569                continue
6570
6571            if color_palette is not None:
6572                primary = label.split(" / ")[0].strip()
6573                if primary in color_palette:
6574                    line.set_color(color_palette[primary])
6575
6576            line.set_alpha(alpha)
6577            line.set_linestyle(linestyle)
6578            handles.append(line)
6579            labels.append(label)
6580
6581        if rebuild_legend and handles:
6582            existing = ax.get_legend()
6583            if existing is not None:
6584                existing.remove()
6585            if legend_outside:
6586                kw = dict(bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.5), loc="center left", frameon=False)
6587            else:
6588                kw = dict(frameon=False)
6589            kw.update(legend_kwargs)
6590            ax.legend(handles, labels, **kw)
6591
6592    return result

Restyle a plot_xy_data() result to use alpha + linestyle for NTC vs targeting, ggplot scale_alpha_manual/scale_linetype_manual style, instead of plot_xy_data's built-in color-tint shading.

Meant for plotting everything on one shared axes with a single flat hue per primary group (e.g. cell_line) rather than faceting: call plot_xy_data with facet_by=None and color_by=['<primary>', 'targeting'] (which labels lines "<primary> / NTC" / "<primary> / Targeting" and tints NTC as a lighter shade of the primary color), then pass the result here to flatten each line back to its primary group's solid color and encode NTC vs targeting as alpha/linestyle instead::

palette = {'CRISPRi': 'steelblue', 'CRISPRa': 'tomato'}
result = model.plot_xy_data(
    'GFI1B',
    facet_by=None,
    color_by=['cell_line', 'targeting'],
    color_palette=palette,
    legend_outside=True,
)
restyle_targeting_lines(result, color_palette=palette, legend_outside=True)

Also works with plain color_by='targeting' (labels are bare "NTC"/"Targeting", no primary-color reset needed -- color_palette=None in that case).

Parameters
  • result (matplotlib Figure, Axes, or array of Axes): Return value of model.plot_xy_data(...).
  • color_palette (dict, optional): {primary_label: color} -- the same dict passed to plot_xy_data(color_palette=...). Used to reset each line to its primary group's flat color, undoing plot_xy_data's NTC tint. If None, colors are left as plot_xy_data drew them (tinted).
  • ntc_alpha, targeting_alpha (float): Alpha for lines whose label contains ntc_label_fragment / targeting_label_fragment respectively.
  • ntc_linestyle, targeting_linestyle (str): Matplotlib linestyle for the same two groups (e.g. 'dashed', 'solid').
  • ntc_label_fragment, targeting_label_fragment (str): Substrings identifying NTC vs targeting lines in their legend label. Lines whose label matches neither are left untouched.
  • rebuild_legend (bool, default True): Regenerate each axes' legend from the restyled lines. Matplotlib legends snapshot line style at creation time, so the original legend won't reflect the restyle otherwise.
  • legend_outside (bool, default False): Match whatever you passed to plot_xy_data(legend_outside=...), so the rebuilt legend is placed the same way.
  • legend_kwargs (dict, optional): Extra kwargs forwarded to the rebuilt legend() call, overriding the defaults (frameon=False, plus bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.5), loc='center left' when legend_outside=True).
Returns
  • The same result object, restyled in place.
Notes

Only Line2D artists (the smoothed trend lines) are restyled -- linestyle has no meaning for scatter points, and plot_xy_data's raw per-cell scatter points are unlabeled and left untouched.

This function does not raise: if result isn't a plt.Axes, plt.Figure, or an array/list containing plt.Axes instances, it resolves to zero axes and silently does nothing. Likewise, any axes found with no lines matching ntc_label_fragment/ targeting_label_fragment are left untouched.
